facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'sassonia': Nell'età della Riforma la Sassonia fu la roccaforte del luteranesimo; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/sassonia/

facts.fact: Revolutionary France annexes the papal city of Avignon and the Comtat Venaissin in 1791.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'avignone': Nel 1791 l'Assemblea nazionale francese proclamò l'annessione di Avignone e del Contado Venassino; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/avignone/

facts.fact: Genoa is occupied by Napoleon's armies in 1797 and becomes the Ligurian Republic under French control until 1814-15.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'genova': la repubblica aristocratica durò fino al 1797, quando fu occupata dalle armate napoleoniche e trasformata in Repubblica democratica ligure; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/genova/

Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'francia': Luigi ottenne ... la Franca Contea (1668; 1678); the county passed with the Burgundian inheritance to the Spanish Habsburgs in 1556; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/francia/
facts.fact: The Franche-Comte passes with the Burgundian inheritance to the Spanish Habsburgs in 1556 and is lost to France in 1668-78.

facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'svizzera' (Bernese expansion in the Vaud after the conquest of the Pays de Vaud in 1536; the canton joined the Confederation); https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/svizzera/
facts.fact: Bern takes the Pays de Vaud from Savoy in 1536; Vaud remains Swiss thereafter.
Under the treaty of Troyes Paris is held by the English from 1420 until Charles VII retakes the city in 1436.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'parigi': P. subì la dominazione inglese dal 1420 al 1436, quando il conestabile Arturo di Richemont entrò in città; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/parigi/

facts.fact: With Paris in English hands the dauphin, later Charles VII, keeps his court and parlement at Bourges until 1429; the court returns to Paris in 1436.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'bourges': Nella prima metà del 15° sec. fu il centro della resistenza realista contro Inglesi e Borgognoni e Carlo VII vi stabilì la corte e il parlamento, rimasti fino al 1429; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/bourges/

facts.fact: Revolutionary France annexes the Genevan republic on 26 April 1798; it remains French until the end of 1813.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'ginevra': Il 26 aprile 1798 G. era annessa alla Francia, cui rimase incorporata fino alla fine del 1813; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/ginevra/

facts.fact: The congress of Vienna (1815) adds Geneva to the Swiss Confederation as a full canton.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'svizzera': Il Congresso di Vienna (1815) ... passata a 22 cantoni con l'adesione di Ginevra, Neuchâtel e Vallese; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/svizzera/

facts.fact: George I moves the Hanoverian court to London in 1714; no elector resides in Hanover for the rest of the period, which under the personal-union rule merges the electorate into Britain.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'hannover': Quando la corte fu trasferita a Londra (1714), nuova residenza della dinastia salita sul trono d'Inghilterra, a Hannover rimasero gli uffici governativi dell'elettorato; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/hannover/

facts.fact: Venice takes over the patriarchate of Aquileia (Friuli) in 1418-20.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'venezia': si impossessò del patriarcato di Aquileia (1418-20); https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/venezia/

facts.fact: The peace of Ferrara (1428) brings Brescia and Bergamo to Venice.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'venezia': La Pace di Ferrara (1428) portò Brescia e Bergamo; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/venezia/

facts.fact: Artois passes to the Habsburgs with the Burgundian inheritance in 1477 and is ceded to France in 1659.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'spagna': con la pace dei Pirenei (1659) furono costretti ad abbandonare alla Francia l'Artois (the county had passed to the Habsburgs with the Burgundian inheritance in 1477); https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/spagna/

facts.fact: The treaty of Utrecht (1713) assigns Sardinia to the Austrian Habsburgs, who exchange it with Savoy for Sicily in 1720.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'sardegna': il trattato di Utrecht (1713) assegnò la Sardegna all'imperatore ... con il trattato di Londra (1718) la Sardegna passò a Vittorio Amedeo II; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/sardegna/

facts.fact: Frederick II annexes Royal (western) Prussia in the First Partition of Poland (1772).
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'polonia': la prima [spartizione] nel 1772 (la Russia ... ; Federico II della Prussia occidentale ...); https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/polonia/

facts.fact: France annexes Piedmont in 1798-99 after forcing Charles Emmanuel IV to abdicate; it is restored to Savoy in 1814.
facts.source: Treccani, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana, entry 'savoia': nel 1798 la Repubblica francese impose a Carlo Emanuele IV di abdicare ... [Piedmont annexed to France]; https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/savoia/

facts.fact: Edward III of England married Philippa, daughter of William (Guillaume) V, Count of Hainaut, Holland and Zeeland, at York Minster on 24 January 1328 after a proxy wedding at Valenciennes in October 1327; a sovereign count's daughter, counted from 1337 to her death in 1369.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m ( 1326, Papal dispensation 30 Aug 1327, by proxy Valenciennes 28 Oct 1327, York Minster 24 Jan 1328 ) PHILIPPA de Hainaut , daughter of GUILLAUME V “le Bon” Comte de"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Edward III and Philippa of Hainault': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/edward-iii-and-philippa-of-hainault

facts.fact: Richard II of England married Anne of Bohemia, daughter of Emperor Charles IV, King of Bohemia, at Westminster on 14, 20 or 22 January 1382; a sovereign's daughter, counted to her death in 1394.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (contract 2 May 1381, St Stephen’s Chapel, Palace of Westminster 14, 20 or 22 Jan 1382) ANNA of Bohemia , daughter of Emperor KARL IV, King of Germany and Bohemia & his fourth wife Elisabeth von Pommern (Prague 11 May"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Richard II and Anne of Bohemia': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/richard-ii-and-anne-of-bohemia

facts.fact: Richard II of England married Isabella, daughter of Charles VI of France, at Calais on 1 November 1396 after contracts and a proxy wedding in Paris in March; a sovereign's daughter, the marriage ended with his deposition in 1399.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly ( contract Paris 9 Mar 1396, by proxy Sainte-Chapelle, Palais Royal, Paris 12 Mar 1396, Calais Saint-Nicolas 1 Nov 1396, not consummated ) as her first husband, ISABELLE de France , daughter of CHARLES VI"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Richard II and Anne of Bohemia' (which notes the 1396 Calais marriage): https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/richard-ii-and-anne-of-bohemia

facts.fact: Henry IV of England married Joan, daughter of Charles II of Navarre and widow of Duke John V of Brittany, by proxy at Eltham in April 1402 and in person at Winchester on 7 February 1403; a sovereign's daughter, counted to Henry's death in 1413 (his first wife Mary de Bohun was an English subject and does not qualify).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Eltham Palace, Kent 3 Apr 1402, in person Winchester Cathedral 7 Feb 1402/3) as her second husband, Infanta doña JUANA de Navarra , widow of JEAN V "le Vaillant" Duke of Brittany , daughter"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Henry IV': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/henry-iv

facts.fact: Henry V of England married Catherine, daughter of Charles VI of France, at Troyes Cathedral on 2 June 1420 under the treaty making him heir to France; a sovereign's daughter, counted to his death in 1422.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Troyes 21 May 1420, Troyes Cathedral 2 Jun 1420) as her first husband, CATHERINE de France , daughter of CHARLES VI King of France & his wife Isabelle [Elisabeth] von Bayern-Ingolstadt (Hôtel de"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Henry V and Catherine de Valois': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/henry-v-and-catherine-de-valois

facts.fact: Henry VI of England married Margaret, daughter of Rene of Anjou, Duke of Lorraine from 1431 and also Count of Provence, at Titchfield on 23 April 1445; Lorraine is taken as the natal state (Provence a defensible alternative), and the marriage ended with his deposition in 1461.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract 22 May 1444, by proxy Nancy, Meurthe-et-Moselle Mar 1445, in person Titchfield, Hampshire 23 Apr 1445) MARGUERITE d’Anjou , daughter of RENÉ Duc d’Anjou Duc de Lorraine Titular King of Sicily and Jerusalem & his first wife"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Henry VI': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/henry-vi

facts.fact: Henry VIII of England married Catherine, daughter of Ferdinand II, king of Aragon and Isabella I, queen of Castile, at Greenwich on 11 June 1509; she was then the widow of his brother Arthur. Natal state is Aragon, Ferdinand's own crown (Castile passed to her sister Joanna in 1504). The marriage ran until its annulment in 1533.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Manor of Bewdley, Worcestershire May 1499, by proxy Bewdley 19 May 1501, in person St Paul’s Cathedral, London 14 Nov 1501) as her first husband, Infanta doña CATALINA de Aragón , daughter of FERNANDO V King of Aragon & his wife Isabel I Queen of Castile (Alcala de Henares 16"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Henry VIII': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/henry-viii

facts.fact: Henry VIII of England married Anne, daughter of John III, Duke of Julich-Cleves-Berg, at Greenwich on 6 January 1540; a sovereign duke's daughter, the unconsummated marriage was annulled on 9 July 1540 (his other wives were English subjects).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m fourthly (Greenwich Palace, Kent 6 Jan 1540, not consummated, annulled 9 Jul 1540) ANNA von Kleve , daughter of JOHANN III Duke of Jülich-Kleve-Berg & his wife Marie von Jülich und Berg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Henry VIII': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/henry-viii

facts.fact: Mary I of England married Philip, son of Emperor Charles V and already Duke of Milan and heir to Spain, at Winchester Cathedral on 25 July 1554; he became King of Spain in 1556, and the marriage ended at Mary's death in 1558 (possible duplicate with the Spanish compilation, where Philip II is himself a listed monarch). Natal state is Castile-Spain: Philip was the only son and heir of Charles V, who in 1554 still ruled both Castile and Aragon.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Winchester Cathedral 25 Jul 1554) as his second wife, Infante don FELIPE of Spain Archduke of Austria , son of Emperor KARL V [CARLOS I King of Aragon and Castile] & his wife"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Mary I': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/mary-i

facts.fact: Charles I of England married Henrietta Maria, daughter of Henry IV of France, by proxy at Notre-Dame on 11 May 1625 and in person at Canterbury on 13 June 1625; a sovereign's daughter, counted to his execution in 1649.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Notre-Dame de Paris 11 May 1625, in person Canterbury Cathedral 13 Jun 1625) HENRIETTE MARIE de France , daughter of HENRI IV King of France & his second wife Maria de'"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Charles I': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/charles-i

facts.fact: Charles II of England married Catherine of Braganza, daughter of King John IV of Portugal, at Portsmouth on 21 May 1662 (a second ceremony followed on 31 May); a sovereign's daughter, counted to his death in 1685.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Winchester 21 May 1662, Church of St Thomas à Becket, Portsmouth 31 May 1662) Infanta dona CATARINA de Portugal , daughter of JOÃO IV King of Portugal & his wife doña Luisa María Francisca Pérez de"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Charles II': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/charles-ii; Royal Museums Greenwich, 'The Entrance of the Lord Ambassador Mountague into the Citty of Lisbone the 28 day of March 1662' (Dirk Stoop), painted for the Braganza match: https://www.rmg.co.uk/collections/objects/rmgc-object-144047

facts.fact: James, Duke of York and later James II, married Mary Beatrice of Modena, daughter of Alfonso IV d'Este, Duke of Modena, by proxy at Modena on 30 September 1673 and in person at Dover in November; the duchy of Modena is meant, and the marriage ended with his deposition in 1688 (his first wife Anne Hyde was an English subject).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Modena 30 Sep 1673, in person Dover 21 Nov 1673) MARIA BEATRICE d'Este Pss of Modena , daughter of ALFONSO IV d’Este Duke of Modena & his wife Laura Martinozzi (Modena"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'James II': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/james-ii

facts.fact: Mary, elder daughter of James II and heiress presumptive from his accession in 1685, married her cousin William, Prince of Orange, at St James's Palace on 4 November 1677; the principality of Orange is meant, since the house of Orange was not sovereign of the Dutch Republic, and the link is counted from 1685 to her death in 1694.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (St James’s Palace 4 Nov 1677) her first cousin, WILLEM III Prins van Oranje Graf von Nassau , son of WILLEM II Prins van Oranje Graf von Nassau, Stadhouder"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Mary II': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/mary-ii

facts.fact: Anne, younger daughter of James II, married Prince George of Denmark, son of Frederick III of Denmark, at St James's Palace on 28 July 1683; she became heiress presumptive when William and Mary took the throne in 1689, and the marriage ended at George's death in 1708.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (St James's Palace, London 28 Jul 1683) GEORG Prince of Denmark , son of FREDERIK III King of Denmark, King of Norway & his wife Sophie"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Queen Anne': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/queen-anne

facts.fact: George, Electoral Prince of Hanover and heir to the British throne from his father's accession in 1714, married Caroline of Brandenburg-Ansbach, daughter of Margrave John Frederick of Ansbach, at Herrenhausen on 22 August 1705; Ansbach was an imperial margraviate, and the link is counted from 1714 to her death in 1737.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Schloß Herrenhausen, Hannover 22 Aug 1705) KAROLINE Markgräfin von Brandenburg-Ansbach , daughter of JOHANN FRIEDRICH Markgraf von Brandenburg-Ansbach & his"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'George II and Caroline': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/george-ii-and-caroline

facts.fact: George III of Great Britain married Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, daughter of Duke Charles Louis Frederick of Mecklenburg-Strelitz, at St James's Palace on 8 September 1761; the Mecklenburg ducal house is meant, and the marriage lasted until her death in 1818.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (St James's Palace 8 Sep 1761) CHARLOTTE Herzogin von Mecklenburg-Strelitz , daughter of KARL LUDWIG FRIEDRICH Herzog von Mecklenburg-Strelit"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'George III': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/george-iii

facts.fact: George, Prince of Wales and later George IV, married his cousin Caroline of Brunswick, daughter of Charles William Ferdinand, Duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbuttel, at St James's Palace on 8 April 1795; a sovereign duke's daughter, the couple separated in 1796.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (St James's Palace 8 Apr 1795) his first cousin, KAROLINE Pss von Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel , daughter of KARL WILHELM FERDINAND Herzog von Braunschweig-Wolfen"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'George IV': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/george-iv

facts.fact: William, Duke of Clarence and heir presumptive from 1827, married Adelaide of Saxe-Meiningen, daughter of Duke George I of Saxe-Meiningen, at Kew on 13 July 1818 (FMG gives 11 July); the Thuringian duchy at Meiningen is meant, and the marriage ran to the 1837 limit.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Kew Palace 11 Jul 1818) ADELHEID Pss von Sachsen-Meiningen , daughter of GEORG I Herzog von Sachsen-Meiningen & his wife Luise"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'William IV': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/william-iv

facts.fact: David II of Scotland married Joan, daughter of Edward II of England, at Berwick on 17 July 1328 under the treaty of Edinburgh-Northampton; a sovereign's daughter, counted from 1337 to her death in 1362 (his second wife Margaret Drummond was a Scottish subject).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Scotland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Berwick-upon-Tweed 17 Jul 1328) JOAN of England , daughter of EDWARD II King of England & his wife Isabelle de France (Tower of London 5 Jul 1321-Hertford Castle 7 Sep 1362, bur Greyfriars Church, Newgate, London). John of Fordun’s Scotichronicon (Continuator) records the marriage at Berwick 17 Jul 1328 of " David filius et heres regis Roberti de Bruce " and " sororem Eadwardi"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SCOTLAND.htm; Royal Family, 'David II (r. 1329-1371)': https://www.royal.uk/david-ii-r-1329-1371

facts.fact: James II of Scotland married Mary, daughter of Arnold, Duke of Guelders, on 3 July 1449 at Holyrood according to the Royal Household account; a sovereign duke's daughter, counted to his death in 1460.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Scotland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (3 Jul 1449) MARIA van Gelre , daughter of ARNOLD Duke of Gelre [Egmond] & his wife Katharina von Kleve"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SCOTLAND.htm; Royal Family, 'James II (r. 1437-1460)' (July 1449 marriage to Mary of Gueldres): https://www.royal.uk/james-ii-r-1437-1460

facts.fact: James III of Scotland married Margaret, daughter of Christian I, King of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, at Edinburgh on 13 July 1469; a sovereign's daughter, counted to her death in 1486.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Scotland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Edinburgh 13 Jul 1469) MARGRETHE of Denmark , daughter of CHRISTIAN I King of Denmark, Norway and Sweden & his wife"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SCOTLAND.htm; Royal Family, 'James III (r. 1460-1488)': https://www.royal.uk/james-iii-r-1460-1488

facts.fact: James IV of Scotland married Margaret Tudor, daughter of Henry VII of England, at Holyrood on 8 August 1503; a sovereign's daughter, counted to his death at Flodden in 1513.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Scotland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (8 Aug 1503) as her first husband, MARGARET Tudor , daughter of HENRY VII King of England & his wife Elizabeth of York (Palace of Westminster 28 Nov"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SCOTLAND.htm; Royal Family, 'James IV (r. 1488-1513)': https://www.royal.uk/james-iv-r1488-1513

facts.fact: James V of Scotland married Madeleine, daughter of Francis I of France, at Notre-Dame de Paris on 1 January 1537 after a contract at Blois in November 1536; a sovereign's daughter, she died at Holyrood in July 1537, so the marriage lasted a single year (his second wife Mary of Guise does not qualify, the Guises being a cadet French noble house).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Scotland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly ( contract Château de Blois, Loir-et-Cher 26 Nov 1536, Notre-Dame de Paris 1 Jan 1537 ) MADELEINE de France , daughter of FRANÇOIS I King of France & his first wife Claude de France ( Château de"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SCOTLAND.htm; Royal Family, 'James V (r. 1513-1542)' (Madeleine died 7 July 1537): https://www.royal.uk/james-v-r1513-1542

facts.fact: Mary, Queen of Scots married Francis, Dauphin of France and son of Henry II, at Notre-Dame de Paris on 24 April 1558 after contracts at Chatillon and the Louvre; he was heir to a sovereign and king from 1559, and the marriage ended at his death in December 1560 (possible duplicate with the French compilation, which also covers Francis II).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Scotland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly ( contract Châtillon 27 Jan 1548, contract Palais du Louvre 19 Apr 1558, Notre-Dame de Paris 24 Apr 1558 ) FRANÇOIS de France Dauphin de Viennois, son of HENRI II King of France & his wife Caterina de’ Medici ( Château de Fontainebleau 19 Jan 1544-Orléans"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SCOTLAND.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'Mary, Queen of Scots': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/mary-queen-of-scots

facts.fact: James VI of Scotland married Anne, daughter of Frederick II of Denmark and Norway, by proxy at Kronborg in August 1589, in person at Oslo on 23 November 1589 and again at Kronborg in January 1590; a sovereign's daughter, counted to her death in 1619, long after he inherited the English throne in 1603.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'England, Kings 1066-1603' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Kronborg Castle Copenhagen 20/24 Aug 1589, in person Oslo 23 Nov 1589, and in person again Kronborg Castle 21 Jan 1590) ANNA Pss of Denmark , daughter of FREDERIK II King of Denmark, King of Norway & his wife Sophie von Mecklenburg-Güstrow"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ENGLAND,%20Kings%201066-1603.htm; Westminster Abbey, 'James I and Anne of Denmark': https://www.westminster-abbey.org/abbey-commemorations/royals/james-i-and-anne-of-denmark

facts.fact: Joan II of Navarre married her cousin Philip of Evreux, son of Louis of France, Count of Evreux, and head of a cadet branch of the French royal house holding the county of Evreux (own 1337 tag); he reigned with her as Philip III of Navarre, and the marriage is counted from 1337 to his death in 1343.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Paris 27 Mar 1318, 18 Jun 1318, Château de Conflans 1329) PHILIPPE d’Evreux , son of LOUIS de France Comte d’Evreux & his wife Marguerite d’Artois (27 Mar 1306-Jerez de la Frontera 23 Sep"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Charles II of Navarre married Joan, daughter of King John II of France, in 1352; a sovereign's daughter, counted to her death in 1373.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Château de Vivier-en-Brie, Coutevroult 12 Feb 1352) JEANNE de France , daughter of JEAN II "le Bon" King of France & his first wife Bonne of Bohemia ("; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Charles III of Navarre, heir from birth in 1361, married Eleanor, daughter of King Henry II of Castile, at Soria on 27 May 1375 after a contract at Burgos in 1373; a sovereign's daughter, counted to her death in 1415 or 1416.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Burgos 1373, Soria 27 May 1375) Infanta doña LEONOR de Castilla y León , daughter of ENRIQUE II of Castile & Juana Manuel de Castilla Señora de Villena, Peñafiel y Escalona"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Blanche I of Navarre, heiress from 1413, married by treaty John of Aragon, son of King Ferdinand I of Aragon and brother of King Alfonso V, at Pamplona on 18 June 1420 after contracts in 1419; he was of the Aragonese royal house and became king in 1458, and the marriage ended at her death in 1441 (her first husband Martin of Sicily died in 1409, before she became heiress, so that marriage is excluded).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by treaty 5 Nov 1419, contract Olite 5 Dec 1419, Pamplona 18 Jun 1420) as his first wife, Infante don JUAN de Aragón , son of FERNANDO I "él de Antequera" King of Aragon & his wife Infanta doña Leonor de Castilla (Medina"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Eleanor of Navarre married Gaston IV, Count of Foix and Viscount of Bearn, under contracts of 1434 and in person in 1441; her father named her heir in 1455, so the link is counted from that year to her death in 1479, Foix being a sovereign county.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract [Tarbes 8 Aug 1434] contract 22 Sep 1434, [consummated early 1442?]) GASTON IV Comte de Foix et de Bigorre, Vicomte de Béarn, son of JEAN III de Grailly Comte de Foix et de"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Henry II of Navarre married Margaret of Angouleme, sister of King Francis I of France, under a contract of 3 January 1526 (Old Style), i.e. early 1527, and the wedding was celebrated in January 1527; she qualifies as a sovereign's sister although her father Charles of Angouleme never reigned, and the marriage ended at her death in 1549.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "e marriage contract between “ Henry…roy de Navarre… ” and “ madame Marguerite de France, seur unique du Roy, duchesse d’Alençon et de Berry… ” is dated 3 Jan 1526 (O.S.) [918] . She was the author of several"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Jeanne III of Navarre, heiress presumptive from birth, married William, Duke of Julich-Cleves-Berg, at Chatellerault on 14 June 1541 after a contract at Anet in July 1540; a sovereign duke, he was the husband of a childless marriage annulled on 12 October 1545.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Château de Châtellerault 14 Jun 1541, not consummated, annulled 12 Oct 1545) WILHELM "der Reiche" Herzog von Kleve, Jülich und Berg , son of JOHANN III "dem Friedfertigen" Herzog von Kleve, Jülich"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Jeanne III of Navarre, heiress presumptive, married Antoine de Bourbon, Duke of Vendome, at Moulins on 20 October 1548; Vendome held its own tag on the 1337 map although a French peerage, and the marriage ended at his death in 1562.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Navarre' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Moulins en Bourbonnais, Allier 20 Oct 1548) ANTOINE de Bourbon Duc de Vendôme , son of CHARLES de Bourbon Duc de Vendôme & his wife Françoise d'Alençon (Château de"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/NAVARRE.htm

facts.fact: Henry III of Navarre (later Henry IV of France) married Margaret of Valois, daughter of King Henry II of France, at Notre-Dame de Paris on 18 August 1572 after a contract at the Louvre the day before; a sovereign's daughter, the link is counted to 1589, when the Navarrese crown passed with him to France (the couple separated in 1578 and the marriage was annulled in 1599).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Capet' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Palais du Louvre 17 Aug 1572, Notre-Dame de Paris 18 Aug 1572, separated 1578, divorced 17 Dec 1599) as his first wife, HENRI de Bourbon King of Navarre , son of ANTOINE de Bourbon Duc de Vendôme, King of Navarre & his wife Jeanne d’Albret Queen of Navarre (Château de"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm

facts.fact: Philip VI of France married Joan "the Lame" of Burgundy at Fontainebleau in July 1313, daughter of Robert II Duke of Burgundy; the marriage was already in being in 1337 and ended with her death on 12 December 1349. Burgundy has its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (contract Sens, Yonne 24 Mar 1303, Fontainebleau end Jul 1313) JEANNE "la Boiteuse" de Bourgogne, daughter of ROBERT II Duke of Burgundy & his wife Agnès de France ([1293/94]-Hôtel de Nesle, Paris 12 Dec 1349, bur église de l'Abbaye royale de Saint-Denis)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_VI_of_France

facts.fact: Philip VI of France married Blanche of Navarre, daughter of Philip III King of Navarre, at Brie-Comte-Robert on 11 January 1350; the marriage lasted only until Philip's death on 22 August 1350.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Brie-Comte-Robert, Seine-et-Marne 11 Jan 1350) Infanta doña BLANCA de Navarra, daughter of FELIPE III “el Bueno” [d’Evreux] King of Navarre & his wife Juana II [de France] Queen of Navarre ([1331]-Château de Neaufles-Saint-Martin, Eure 5 Oct 1398"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_VI_of_France

facts.fact: John II of France married Bonne (Jutta) of Luxembourg, daughter of John King of Bohemia, at Melun on 28 July 1332; the marriage was in being in 1337 and ended with her death in September 1349.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Notre-Dame de Melun, Seine-et-Marne 28 Jul 1332) GUTA of Bohemia, daughter of JAN I King of Bohemia [JEAN I Comte de Luxembourg] & his first wife Eliska [Elisabeth] of Bohemia [Přemyslid] (Prague 20 May 1315-Abbaye de Maubuisson, Saint-Ouen l'Aumône, Val-d'Oise 3 or 11 Sep 1349"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_II_of_France

facts.fact: John II of France married Joan I, sovereign Countess of Auvergne and Boulogne in her own right, at Sainte-Gemme on 9 February 1350; she died on 29 September 1360. Auvergne carries its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Sainte-Gemme, Feucherolles, Yvelines 9 Feb 1350) as her second husband, JEANNE Ctss d'Auvergne et de Boulogne, widow of PHILIPPE de Bourgogne "Monsieur" Comte d'Artois [Capet], daughter of GUILLAUME [XI] Comte d'Auvergne et de Boulogne & his wife Marguerite d'Evreux (8 May 1326-Vadans"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_II_of_France

facts.fact: Charles V of France, then Dauphin, married Joanna of Bourbon, daughter of Peter I Duke of Bourbon, at Tain-en-Viennois on 8 April 1350; Bourbon is an appanage duchy with its own 1337 tag. The marriage ended with her death on 6 February 1378.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Lyon Jul 1349, Tain-en-Viennois, Drôme 8 Apr 1350) JEANNE de Bourbon, daughter of PIERRE I Duc de Bourbon & his wife Isabelle de Valois (Château du Bois de Vincennes 3 Feb 1339-Hôtel de Saint-Pol, Paris 6 Feb 1378, bur église de l'Abbaye royale de Saint-Denis)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V_of_France

facts.fact: Charles VI of France married Isabeau (Elisabeth) of Bavaria-Ingolstadt, daughter of Stephen II Duke of Bavaria-Ingolstadt, at Amiens on 17 July 1385; the marriage ran to his death on 21 October 1422.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Cathedral of Amiens 17 Jul 1385 or Tournai [24] Aug 1385) ELISABETH von Bayern-Ingolstadt, daughter of STEFAN II Duke of Bavaria-Ingolstadt & his first wife Taddea Visconti ([1369/70]-Paris 24 or 30 Sep 1435, bur église de l'Abbaye royale de Saint-Denis)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_VI_of_France

facts.fact: Charles VII of France, then Dauphin, married Marie of Anjou, daughter of Louis II Duke of Anjou and titular King of Naples, at Tours on 2 June 1422; he succeeded in October 1422 and the marriage ran to his death in 1461. Anjou has its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Palais du Louvre 18 Dec 1413, Tours 2 Jun 1422) MARIE d'Anjou, daughter of LOUIS II Duc d'Anjou Titular King of Naples, Sicily and Jerusalem & his wife Infanta doña Violanta de Aragón (Angers 14 Oct 1404-Abbaye de Chateliers-en-Poitou, near Saint-Maxent, Deux-Sèvres 29 Nov 1463"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_VII_of_France

facts.fact: Louis XI of France, then Dauphin, married Margaret of Scotland, daughter of James I King of Scots, at Tours on 25 June 1436; she died on 16 August 1445.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (contract Perth, Scotland 19 Jul 1428, contract Chinon, Indre-et-Loire 30 Oct 1428, Cathédrale de Tours 25 Jun 1436)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XI

facts.fact: Louis XI of France, then Dauphin, married Charlotte of Savoy, daughter of Louis I Duke of Savoy, at Chambery on 9 March 1451 against his father's wish; she outlived him and died on 1 December 1483.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (contract Genève, couvent des Cordeliers, Château de Chambéry 9 Mar 1451) CHARLOTTE de Savoie, daughter of LOUIS I Duke of Savoy & his wife Anne Pss of Cyprus (11 Nov 1441-Amboise, Indre-et-Loire 1 Dec 1483, bur Cléry, église de Notre-Dame)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XI

facts.fact: Charles VIII of France married Anne, sovereign Duchess of Brittany, at Langeais on 6 December 1491; the marriage ended with his death on 7 April 1498. Brittany has its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Château de Langeais, Indre-et-Loire 6 Dec 1491, contract Langeais 13 Dec 1491) as her second husband, ANNE Dss of Brittany, formerly wife of MAXIMILIAN King of the Romans Archduke of Austria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_VIII_of_France

facts.fact: Louis XII of France married Anne, sovereign Duchess of Brittany, at Nantes on 7 January 1499 after the annulment of his first marriage; she died on 9 January 1514.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (contract Etampes 18 Aug 1498[1332], Papal dispensation 13 Sep 1498, Château de Nantes 7 Jan 1499)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XII

facts.fact: Louis XII of France married Mary, daughter of Henry VII King of England, at Abbeville on 9 October 1514; he died on 1 January 1515.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (contract London 7 Aug 1514, by proxy Greyfriars Church, Greenwich Palace 13 Aug 1514, by proxy église des Célestins Paris 2 Sep 1514, contract 14 Sep 1514, in person Abbeville Cathedral, Somme 9 Oct 1514)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XII

facts.fact: Francis I of France married Eleanor of Austria, widow of Manuel I of Portugal and sister of Emperor Charles V, at Villeneuve-de-Marsan on 7 August 1530; the marriage ran to his death on 31 March 1547. Natal state is Castile, the crown of her brother Charles I of Spain.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Torrelaguna, Castile 20 Mar 1530, in person Abbaye de Saint-Laurent de Beyries, near Villeneuve-de-Marsan, Landes 7 Aug 1530)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_I_of_France

facts.fact: Henry II of France, then Duke of Orleans, married Catherine de' Medici, daughter of Lorenzo II de' Medici ruler of Florence, at Marseille on 28 October 1533; he became Dauphin in August 1536, so the link is counted from 1536 to his death on 10 July 1559.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Château d'Anet, Eure-et-Loir 24 Apr 1531, contract Marseille 27 Oct 1533, Marseille Cathedral 28 Oct 1533)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_II_of_France

facts.fact: Mary Queen of Scots married Francis II of France at Notre-Dame de Paris on 24 April 1558; both were reigning sovereigns at the wedding, and the task assigns the actor to Scotland. The marriage ended with his death on 5 December 1560. Possible duplicate with the Scotland compilation (mar_sco_mary_1558_france).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Châtillon 27 Jan 1548, contract Palais du Louvre 19 Apr 1558, Notre-Dame de Paris 24 Apr 1558) as her first husband, MARY I Queen of Scots, daughter of JAMES V King of Scotland & his second wife Marie de Lorraine (Linlithgow Palace 7/8 Dec 1542-executed Fotheringay Castle"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary,_Queen_of_Scots

facts.fact: Charles IX of France married Elisabeth of Austria, daughter of Emperor Maximilian II, at Mezieres-en-Champagne on 26 November 1570; the marriage ended with his death in 1574.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract Madrid 14 Jan 1570, by proxy Speyer 22 Oct 1570, in person Notre-Dame de l'Espérance, Mézières-en-Champagne 26 Nov 1570)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_IX_of_France

facts.fact: Henry IV of France married Marie de' Medici, daughter of Francesco I Grand Duke of Tuscany, at Lyon on 27 December 1600; the marriage ended with his assassination on 14 May 1610. Florence (FLO) is the 1337 tag of the Medici state.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Florence 5 Oct 1600, in person cathedral of Saint-Jean, Lyon 27 Dec 1600) MARIA de’ Medici Pss of Tuscany, daughter of FRANCESCO I Grand Duke of Tuscany & his first wife Johanna Archduchess of Austria (Florence 26 Apr 1575-Köln 3 Jul 1642, bur Saint-Denis)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_IV_of_France

facts.fact: Louis XIII of France married Anne of Austria, daughter of Philip III King of Spain, at Bordeaux on 24 November 1615; the marriage ran to his death on 14 May 1643.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Burgos 18 Oct 1615, in person Bordeaux 24 Nov 1615) Infanta doña ANA of Spain, daughter of FELIPE III King of Spain & his wife Margareta Archduchess of Austria (Valladolid 22 Sep 1601-Louvre 20 Jan 1666, bur Saint-Denis)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIII

facts.fact: Louis XIV of France married Maria Theresa of Spain, daughter of Philip IV King of Spain, at Saint-Jean-de-Luz on 9 June 1660; the marriage ended with her death on 30 July 1683.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (by proxy Fuenterrabia 3 Jun 1660 in person Saint-Jean-de-Luz 9 Jun 1660) Infanta doña MARÍA TERESA of Spain, daughter of FELIPE IV King of Spain & his wife Elisabeth de France (Madrid 20 Sep 1638-Versailles 30 Jul 1683, bur Saint-Denis). m secondly (in secret, Versailles [1683/84])"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XIV

facts.fact: Louis XV of France married Marie Leszczynska, daughter of Stanislaw I Leszczynski former King of Poland, at Fontainebleau on 5 September 1725; Poland still existed under another king, so the natal state is Poland. She died on 24 June 1768.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Strasbourg 15 Aug 1725, in person Fontainebleau 5 Sep 1725) MARIA Leszczynska Pss of Poland, daughter of STANISLAS I Leszczynski ex-King of Poland & his wife Katarzyna Ctss Opalinska (Wroclaw (Breslau) 23 Jun 1703-Versailles 24 Jun 1768, bur Saint-Denis)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XV

facts.fact: Louis XVI of France, then Dauphin, married Marie Antoinette, daughter of Emperor Francis I, at Versailles on 16 May 1770; the link ends with the abolition of the monarchy in September 1792.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Vienna 18 Apr 1770, in person Versailles 16 May 1770) MARIA ANTONIA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor FRANZ I & his wife Maria Theresia Archduchess of Austria, Queen of Bohemia, King of Hungary (Vienna 2 Nov 1755-guillotined Paris 16 Oct 1793"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XVI

facts.fact: Napoleon I, Emperor of the French, married Marie Louise, daughter of Emperor Francis I of Austria, in Paris on 1-2 April 1810; the link ends with his abdication on 11 April 1814. His first wife Josephine was a French subject and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Vienna 11 Mar 1810, in person Saint-Cloud (civ) 1 Apr 1810, Palais du Louvre, Paris (rel) 2 Apr 1810)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napoleon

facts.fact: Louis XVIII of France, then Count of Provence, married Marie Josephine of Savoy, daughter of Victor Amadeus III King of Sardinia, at Versailles on 14 May 1771; he became heir presumptive on Louis XVI's accession in 1774, so the link is counted from 1774 to her death in 1810.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "France, Capetian Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Turin 21 Apr 1771, in person Versailles 14 May 1771) MARIA GIUSEPPINA LUIGIA di Savoia Pss of Sardinia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CAPET.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_XVIII

facts.fact: Charles X of France, then Count of Artois, married Marie Therese of Savoy, daughter of Victor Amadeus III King of Sardinia, at Versailles on 16 August 1773; he became heir presumptive to the royal claim only in 1795, so the link runs from 1795 to her death in 1805.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Versailles 16 Aug 1773) CHARLES Philippe de France Comte d'Artois, son of LOUIS Dauphin de France & his second wife Maria Josepha Pss of Saxony (Versailles 9 Oct 1757- Schloß Graffenberg, Görz [Gorizia, now in Italy] 6 Nov 1836, bur Santa Maria del Annunziazione, Castagnavizza [Kostanjevica na Krasu"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_X_of_France

facts.fact: Louis-Philippe I, King of the French, had married Maria Amalia of Naples and Sicily, daughter of Ferdinand I King of the Two Sicilies, at Palermo on 25 November 1809; he came to the throne in August 1830 and the link is counted to the 1837 horizon.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Palermo 25 Nov 1809) LOUIS PHILIPPE d’Orléans Duc d’Orléans, son of PHILIPPE d’Orléans Duc de Chartres [later Duc d’Orléans] & his wife Louise Marie Adélaïde de Bourbon Mademoiselle de Penthièvre (Palais Royal 6 Oct 1773-Claremont House, near Esher, Surrey 26 Aug 1850)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Philippe_I

facts.fact: Robert I of Naples married Sancha of Mallorca, daughter of James II King of Mallorca, in 1304; the marriage was in being in 1337 and ended with Robert's death on 19 January 1343.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Perpignan 17 Jun 1304 in person Chapelle des Hospitaliers, Palais royal de Collioure, Pyrénées-Orientales 20 Sep 1304)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_of_Naples

facts.fact: Joanna I of Naples married Andrew of Hungary, son of Charles I King of Hungary, at Naples on 26 September 1333; the marriage was in being in 1337 and ended with his murder on 18 September 1345.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (contract 8 Nov 1332, Santa Chiara Naples 26 Sep 1333, consummated 22/23 Jan 1344) ANDRÁS Prince of Hungary, son of KÁROLY I King of Hungary [Anjou-Capet] & his third wife Elźbieta of Poland (30 Nov 1327-murdered San Pietro a Maiella, near Aversa 18/19 Sep 1345, bur Naples Cathedral)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_I_of_Naples

facts.fact: Joanna I of Naples married Otto Duke of Brunswick-Grubenhagen at Naples on 25 September 1376; he was an Imperial prince of a house with its own 1337 tag. The link ends with her deposition in 1380.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m fourthly (contract Avignon 28 Dec 1375, Château-Neuf, Naples 25 Sep 1376) as his second wife, OTTO Herzog von Braunschweig-Grubenhagen, son of HEINRICH “dem Griechischen” Herzog von Braunschweig-Grubenhagen & his first wife Jutta von Brandenburg (1320-Castle of Foggia, Taranto [Nov 1399/Feb 1400]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_I_of_Naples

facts.fact: Ladislaus of Naples married Mary of Lusignan, daughter of James I King of Cyprus, in February 1403; she died on 4 September 1404.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly ([13/28] Feb 1403) MARIE of Cyprus, daughter of JACQUES I King of Cyprus & his wife Helvis von Braunschweig ([Genoa 1381]-Naples 4 Sep 1404, bur Naples San Domenico). The Lignages d'Outremer name (in order) "Marietta, Isabella, Civa e Agnese" as the four daughters of "Giacomo"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladislaus_of_Naples

facts.fact: Joanna II of Naples, then heir of her brother Ladislaus, married William Duke of Austria at Vienna in 1401; the marriage ended with his death on 15 July 1406 (possible duplicate with the Habsburg compilation).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Vienna [13 Oct/13 Nov] 1401) WILHELM Duke of Styria and Inner Austria, son of LEOPOLD III Duke of Austria & his wife Verde Visconti (1370-Vienna 15 Jul 1406, bur Vienna). The Necrologium Austriacum refers to the wife of Duke Wilhelm as "kunig Karl tochter von Pulan"[996]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_II_of_Naples

facts.fact: Rene of Anjou married Isabella, daughter and heiress of Charles I Duke of Lorraine, at Nancy on 24 October 1420; he became King of Naples in 1435 and was expelled in 1442, so the link is counted from 1435 to 1442.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Anjou: Comtes, Ducs d'Anjou" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (contract Château de Foug, Meurthe-et-Moselle 20 Mar 1420, Nancy 24 Oct 1420) ISABELLE de Lorraine, daughter and heiress of CHARLES I Duke of Lorraine & his wife Margareta von Bayern ([1400]-Château d'Angers 28 Feb 1453, bur Angers Cathédrale Saint-Maurice)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ANJOU,%20MAINE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_of_Anjou

facts.fact: Ferdinand I of Naples married Joanna of Aragon, daughter of John II King of Aragon and Navarre, on 14 September 1476; the marriage ran to his death on 25 January 1494.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (14 Sep 1476) Infanta doña JUANA de Aragón, daughter of JUAN II King of Aragon and Navarre & his second wife Juana Enríquez Señora de Casarrubios del Monte y Arroyojolinos (Barcelona [1454]-Naples 9 Jan 1517)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_Naples

facts.fact: Alfonso II of Naples, then Duke of Calabria and heir, married Ippolita Maria Sforza, daughter of Francesco I Sforza Duke of Milan, at Milan on 10 October 1465; she died on 20 August 1484.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Milan 10 Oct 1465) IPPOLITA MARIA Sforza, daughter of FRANCESCO I ALESSANDRO Sforza Duke of Milan Conte di Pavia & his wife Bianca Maria Visconti (Cremona 18 Apr 1446-Naples 20 Aug 1484)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_II_of_Naples

facts.fact: Charles of Bourbon, King of Naples and Sicily, married Maria Amalia, daughter of Frederick Augustus II Elector of Saxony and King of Poland, by proxy at Dresden on 9 May 1738 and in person at Gaeta on 19 June 1738; the link ends when he ceded Naples on becoming King of Spain in 1759. Dresden stands for the Saxon electorate.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Castile & Leon, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Dresden 9 May 1738 in person Gaeta 19 Jun 1738) MARIA AMALIA Pss of Saxony, daughter of FRIEDRICH AUGUST II Duke of Saxony [AUGUST III King of Poland] & his wife Maria Josepha Archduchess of Austria (Dresden 24 Nov 1724-Buen Retiro, Madrid 27 Sep 1760, bur El Escorial)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_III_of_Spain

facts.fact: Ferdinand IV of Naples (Ferdinand III of Sicily) married Maria Carolina, daughter of Emperor Francis I and Maria Theresa, by proxy at Vienna on 7 April 1768 and in person at Caserta on 12 May 1768; she died on 8 September 1814, the link being counted through the 1806-1815 exile in Sicily.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (by proxy Vienna 7 Apr 1768 in person Caserta 12 May 1768) MARIA KAROLINA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor FRANZ I & his wife Maria Theresia Archduchess of Austria, Queen of Bohemia, King of Hungary (Schönbrunn 13 Aug 1752-Schloß Hetzendorf 8 Sep 1814, bur Kapuzinergruft Vienna)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_the_Two_Sicilies

facts.fact: Joachim Murat married Caroline Bonaparte, sister of Napoleon I Emperor of the French, at Mortefontaine on 20 January 1800; he became King of Naples on 1 August 1808, so the link runs from 1808 until he lost the throne in May 1815. Natal state is France, her brother's empire.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Mortefontaine (civ) 20 Jan 1800, Paris (rel) 4 Jan 1802) [as her first husband,] CAROLINE Bonaparte, daughter of CARLO Buonaparte & his wife Maria Letizia Ramolino (Ajaccio 25 Mar 1782-Florence 18 May 1839). Princesse française (Imperial Highness)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joachim_Murat

facts.fact: Francis I of the Two Sicilies, then heir as Duke of Calabria, married Maria Clementina, daughter of Emperor Leopold II, by proxy at Vienna on 19 September 1790 (the binding marriage) and in person at Foggia on 25 June 1797; she died on 15 November 1801.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (by proxy Vienna 19 Sep 1790, in person Foggia 25 Jun 1797) his first cousin, MARIE KLEMENTINE Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor LEOPOLD II, Archduke of Austria & his wife Infanta doña María Luisa de Borbón y Sajonia (Poggio Imperiale 24 Apr 1777-Naples 15 Nov 1801"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_I_of_the_Two_Sicilies

facts.fact: Francis I of the Two Sicilies, then heir, married Maria Isabella, daughter of Charles IV King of Spain, at Naples on 6 October 1802; the marriage ran to his death on 8 November 1830.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Barcelona 6 Jul 1802, in person Naples 6 Oct 1802) as her first husband, his first cousin, Infanta doña MARÍA ISABEL de Borbón y Borbón, daughter of CARLOS IV King of Spain and his wife donna Maria Luisa di Borbone Pss of Parma (Madrid 6 Jul 1789-Portici Palace, Naples 13 Sep 1848)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_I_of_the_Two_Sicilies

facts.fact: Ferdinand II of the Two Sicilies married Maria Cristina of Savoy, daughter of Victor Emmanuel I King of Sardinia, at Voltri on 21 November 1832; she died on 31 January 1836.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Sicily/Naples, Counts & Kings" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Voltri 21 Nov 1832) MARIA CRISTINA di Savoia Pss of Sardinia, daughter of VITTORIO EMANUELE I King of Sardinia & his wife Maria Theresia Archduchess of Austria Principessa di Carrara and Duchessa di Massa (Cagliari 14 Nov 1812-Caserta 31 Jan 1836, bur Basilica Santa Chiara, Naples)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SICILY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_II_of_the_Two_Sicilies

facts.fact: Charles Emmanuel III of Sardinia married Anna Christina of Sulzbach, daughter of Theodore Count Palatine of Sulzbach, an Imperial immediate principality, in person at Vercelli on 15 March 1722; she died on 12 March 1723.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (by proxy 16 Feb 1722, in person Vercelli 15 Mar 1722) ANNA CHRISTINA LUISE Pfalzgräfin von Sulzbach, daughter of THEODOR Pfalzgraf und Herzog von Sulzbach & his wife Maria Eleonora Amalie Landgraf von Hessen-Rheinfels-Rotenburg (Sulzbach 5 Feb 1704-Turin 12 Mar 1723"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Emmanuel_III_of_Sardinia

facts.fact: Charles Emmanuel III of Sardinia married Polyxena of Hesse-Rotenburg, daughter of Ernest Leopold Landgrave of Hesse-Rotenburg, an Imperial immediate landgraviate, at Thorn on 20 August 1724; she died on 13 January 1735.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Thorn 20 Aug 1724) POLYXENA CHRISTINA Johannetta Landgräfin von Hessen-Rheinfels, daughter of ERNST LEOPOLD Landgraf von Hessen-Rheinfels & his wife Eleonore Gräfin zu Löwenstein-Wertheim-Rochefort (Langenschwalbach 21 Sep 1706-Turin 13 Jan 1735, bur Turin Basilica La Superga)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Emmanuel_III_of_Sardinia

facts.fact: Charles Emmanuel III of Sardinia married Elisabeth Therese of Lorraine, daughter of Leopold Joseph Duke of Lorraine, at Chambery on 1 April 1737; she died on 3 July 1741.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Chambéry 1 Apr 1737) ELISABETH THERESE de Lorraine, daughter of LEOPOLD JOSEPH Duke of Lorraine & his wife Elisabeth Charlotte d’Orléans (Lunéville 15 Oct 1711-Turin 3 Jul 1741, bur Turin Basilica La Superga). Carlo Emanuele & his first wife had one child: 1"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Emmanuel_III_of_Sardinia

facts.fact: Victor Amadeus III of Sardinia married Maria Antonia Fernanda of Spain, daughter of Philip V King of Spain, in person at Oulx on 31 May 1750; she died on 19 September 1785.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Madrid 12 Apr 1750, in person Oulx 31 May 1750) Infanta doña María ANTONIA Fernanda de Borbón y Farnesio, daughter of FELIPE V King of Spain & his second wife Elisabetta Maria Farnese Pss of Parma [Isabel Farnesio] (Seville 17 Nov 1729-Moncalieri 19 Sep 1785, bur Turin Basilica La Superga)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Amadeus_III

facts.fact: Charles Emmanuel IV of Sardinia, then Prince of Piedmont and heir, married Clotilde of France, sister of Louis XVI, at Chambery on 6 September 1775; she died on 7 March 1802.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Versailles 21 Aug 1775, in person Chambéry 6 Sep 1775) CLOTILDE de France, daughter of LOUIS Dauphin de France & his second wife Maria Josepha Pss of Saxony (Versailles 23 Sep 1759-Naples 7 Mar 1802, bur Santa Caterina, Naples)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Emmanuel_IV

facts.fact: Victor Emmanuel I of Sardinia married Maria Theresa of Austria-Este at Turin on 25 April 1789; she succeeded her mother in 1790 as sovereign Duchess of Massa and Princess of Carrara, and so qualifies as a reigning sovereign in her own right. He became heir in 1796, so the link runs from 1796 to his abdication in 1821.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Turin 25 Apr 1789) MARIA THERESIA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of FERDINAND Archduke of Austria [later FERDINANDO Duke of Modena] & his wife Maria Beatrice d’Este Pss of Modena (Milan 1 Nov 1773-Genoa 29 Mar 1832, bur Basilica La Superga Turin)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Emmanuel_I

facts.fact: Charles Felix of Sardinia, then heir presumptive, married Maria Cristina of Naples and Sicily, daughter of Ferdinand I King of the Two Sicilies, at Turin on 6 April 1807; the marriage ran to his death on 27 April 1831.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Palermo 7 Mar 1807, in person Turin 6 Apr 1807) MARIA CRISTINA di Borbone Pss of Naples and Sicily, daughter of FERDINANDO II ex-King of Naples [FERDINANDO III ex-King of Sicily] [later restored"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Felix_of_Sardinia

facts.fact: Charles Albert of Sardinia married Maria Theresa of Austria, daughter of Ferdinand III Grand Duke of Tuscany, at Florence on 30 September 1817; he became heir presumptive in 1821 and king in 1831, so the link runs from 1821 to the 1837 horizon.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "Savoy" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Florence 30 Sep 1817) MARIA TERESA Archduchess of Austria, Pss of Tuscany, daughter of FERDINANDO III Grand Duke of Tuscany & his wife donna Luisa di Borbone Pss of Naples and Sicily (Vienna 21 Mar 1801-Turin 12 Jan 1855)."; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAVOY.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Albert_of_Sardinia

facts.fact: Alfonso XI of Castile married Maria of Portugal, daughter of Afonso IV King of Portugal, at Alfayete in September 1328; the marriage predates the horizon and is counted from 1337 until his death before Gibraltar on 26 March 1350. His first wife Constanza Manuel was a Castilian nobleman's daughter and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (contract 26 Mar 1327, Alfayete Sep 1328) his first cousin, Infanta dona MARIA de Portugal, daughter of AFONSO IV King of Portugal"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_XI_of_Castile

facts.fact: Peter I of Castile married Blanche of Bourbon, daughter of Peter I Duke of Bourbon, at Valladolid on 3 June 1353; Bourbon is a separate polity with its own 1337 tag, and the marriage ran to her death in 1361, the king's 1354 repudiation having been condemned by Pope Innocent VI and never lawfully dissolving it. Juana de Castro and Maria de Padilla were Castilian subjects and do not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (contract 1351, by proxy Abbaye de Preuilly 9 Jul 1352 in person Valladolid 3 Jun 1353, purportedly divorced 1354) BLANCHE de Bourbon, daughter of PIERRE I Duc de Bourbon Comte de Clermont et de La Marche"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_of_Castile

facts.fact: John I of Castile married Eleanor of Aragon, daughter of Peter IV King of Aragon, at Soria on 18 June 1375 while he was heir to Henry II; the marriage ran to her death in childbirth on 13 September 1382.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Betrothed 12 Apr 1374, Soria 18 Jun 1375) Infanta doña LEONOR de Aragón, daughter of PEDRO IV "el Ceremonioso" King of Aragon"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_I_of_Castile

facts.fact: John I of Castile married Beatrice of Portugal, daughter of Ferdinand I King of Portugal, at Elvas on 14 May 1383; he took his son's intended bride himself after his first wife died, and the marriage ran to his death on 9 October 1390.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Elvas 14 May 1383) Infanta dona BRITES de Portugal, daughter of FERNANDO I King of Portugal & his wife Leonor Téllez de Meneses"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_I_of_Castile

facts.fact: Henry III of Castile married Catherine of Lancaster at Palencia in September 1388; her father John of Gaunt never reigned, but her half-brother Henry IV became King of England in 1399, and the rule accepts a sibling who reigned before, at or after the wedding, so the link runs from 1388 to Henry's death in 1406.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Palencia Sep 1388, consummated Madrid Feb 1393) KATHARINE of Lancaster, daughter of JOHN of Gaunt Duke of Lancaster & his second wife [Infanta] doña Constanza de Castilla y León"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_III_of_Castile

facts.fact: John II of Castile married his cousin Maria of Aragon, daughter of Ferdinand I King of Aragon, at Avila on 4 August 1420; the marriage ran to her death on 18 February 1445. His second wife Isabella of Portugal was a granddaughter of King John I through a son who never reigned and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Avila 4 Aug 1420) his first cousin, Infanta doña MARÍA de Aragón, daughter of FERNANDO I "él de Antequera" King of Aragon"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_II_of_Castile

facts.fact: Henry IV of Castile, then Prince of Asturias, married Blanche of Navarre at Valladolid on 15 September 1440; her father was reigning King of Navarre and later of Aragon, and the marriage was annulled in 1453, which ends the link.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Valladolid 15 Sep 1440, annulled 1453) Infanta doña BLANCA de Navarra y Aragón, daughter of Infante don JUAN de Aragón, JUAN King of Navarre [later JUAN II King of Aragon]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_IV_of_Castile

facts.fact: Henry IV of Castile married Joan of Portugal, daughter of Edward I King of Portugal, at Córdoba on 20 May 1455; the marriage ran to his death on 11 December 1474.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Córdoba 20 May 1455) Infanta dona JUANA de Portugal, daughter of DUARTE I King of Portugal & his wife Infanta doña Leonor de Aragón"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_IV_of_Castile

facts.fact: Isabella I of Castile married Ferdinand, heir and later King of Aragon, at Valladolid on 19 October 1469; she had been recognised heiress of Castile at Toros de Guisando in 1468, so the link counts from the wedding to her death on 26 November 1504. One fact only, assigned to Castile.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Valladolid 19 Oct 1469) as his first wife, Infante don FERNANDO de Aragón, son of JUAN II King of Aragon and Navarre"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabella_I_of_Castile

facts.fact: Joanna of Castile married Philip of Habsburg, son of Emperor Maximilian I, at Lille on 20 October 1496; she became heiress presumptive of Castile only when her nephew Miguel da Paz died on 19 July 1500, so the link runs from 1500 to Philip's death at Burgos on 25 September 1506.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Lille 20 Oct 1496) PHILIPP Archduke of Austria, son of Emperor MAXIMILIAN I Archduke of Austria & his first wife Marie Dss de Bourgogne"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ARAGON%20%26%20CATALONIA.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_of_Castile

facts.fact: Charles I of Castile and Aragon, Emperor Charles V, married his cousin Isabella of Portugal, daughter of Manuel I King of Portugal, at Seville on 10 March 1526; the marriage ran to her death on 1 May 1539.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Sevilla 10 Mar 1526) Infanta dona ISABEL de Portugal, daughter of MANOEL I King of Portugal & his wife Infanta doña María de Aragón"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_V,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Philip II of Spain married Maria Manuela of Portugal, daughter of John III King of Portugal, at Salamanca on 12 November 1543; she died on 12 July 1545.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Salamanca 12 Nov 1543) Infanta dona MARIA de Portugal, daughter of JOÃO III King of Portugal & his wife Katharina Archduchess of Austria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain

facts.fact: Philip, heir to Spain, married Mary I Queen of England at Winchester Cathedral on 24/25 July 1554; the bride was the reigning sovereign at the wedding and the groom was not yet king of Spain, so under the shared rule the actor is England, and this is a possible duplicate with the England compilation (mar_eng_mary1_1554_spain). The link ends at Mary's death on 17 November 1558.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Winchester Cathedral 24 Jul 1554) MARY I Queen of England, daughter of HENRY VIII King of England & his first wife Infanta doña Catalina de Aragón"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_I_of_England

facts.fact: Philip II of Spain married Elisabeth of Valois, daughter of Henry II King of France, by proxy at Notre-Dame in Paris on 22 June 1559 and in person at Guadalajara on 2 February 1560; the binding proxy marriage dates the link, which ran to her death in childbirth on 3 October 1568.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (contract Palais du Louvre 20 Jun 1559, by proxy Notre-Dame de Paris 22 Jun 1559, in person Guadalajara 2 Feb 1560) ELISABETH de Valois Pss de France, daughter of HENRI II King of France"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain

facts.fact: Philip II of Spain married his niece Anna of Austria, daughter of Emperor Maximilian II, at Segovia on 12 November 1570; she died on 26 October 1580.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m fourthly (Segovia 12 Nov 1570) his niece, ANNA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor MAXIMILIAN II Archduke of Austria, King of Bohemia & Hungary"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_II_of_Spain

facts.fact: Philip III of Spain married Margaret of Austria, daughter of Archduke Charles II of Inner Austria of the Habsburg line, at Valencia on 18 April 1599; she died on 3 October 1611.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Valencia 18 Apr 1599) MARGARETA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of KARL Archduke of Austria, Duke in Styria, Carinthia & Carniola"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_III_of_Spain

facts.fact: Philip IV of Spain married Elisabeth of France, daughter of Henry IV King of France, at Bordeaux on 25 November 1615; she died on 6 October 1644.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Bordeaux 25 Nov 1615) ELISABETH de France dite Madame, daughter of HENRI IV King of France & his second wife Maria de' Medici Pss of Tuscany"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_IV_of_Spain

facts.fact: Philip IV of Spain married his niece Mariana of Austria, daughter of Emperor Ferdinand III, at Madrid on 8 November 1649; the marriage ran to his death on 17 September 1665.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Madrid 8 Nov 1649) his niece, MARIA ANNA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor FERDINAND III Archduke of Austria, King of Bohemia and Hungary"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_IV_of_Spain

facts.fact: Charles II of Spain married Maria Anna of Pfalz-Neuburg, daughter of Philip William Elector Palatine, at San Diego near Valladolid on 14 May 1690; the Electorate is an Imperial immediate principality, and the marriage ran to his death on 1 November 1700. His first wife Marie Louise of Orleans, daughter of a duke of Orleans who never reigned, does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (San Diego near Valladolid 14 May 1690) MARIA ANNA Pss von Pfalz-Neuburg, daughter of PHILIPP WILHELM Elector Palatine, Pfalzgraf und Herzog von Neuburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_II_of_Spain

facts.fact: Philip V of Spain married Maria Luisa of Savoy, daughter of Victor Amadeus II Duke of Savoy, by proxy at Turin on 11 September 1701 and in person at Figueras on 3 November 1701; she died on 14 February 1714.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (by proxy Turin 11 Sep 1701, in person Figueras 3 Nov 1701) MARIE LOUISE GABRIELLE de Savoie, daughter of VICTOR AMEDEE II Duke of Savoy [later VITTORIO AMEDEO I King of Sardinia]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_V_of_Spain

facts.fact: Philip V of Spain married Elisabeth Farnese, daughter of Odoardo Hereditary Prince of Parma and the senior heiress of the ducal house, by proxy at Parma on 16 September 1714 and in person at Guadalajara on 24 December 1714; the marriage ran to his death on 9 July 1746.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Parma 16 Sep 1714, in person Guadalajara 24 Dec 1714) ELISABETTA MARIA Farnese Pss of Parma, daughter of ODOARDO Hereditary Prince of Parma"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philip_V_of_Spain

facts.fact: Ferdinand VI of Spain, then Prince of Asturias and heir, married Barbara of Portugal, daughter of John V King of Portugal, at Badajoz on 20 January 1729; she died on 27 August 1758.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Badajoz 20 Jan 1729) Infanta dona MARIA BARBARA de Bragança e Austria, daughter of JOÃO V King of Portugal & his wife Maria Anna Josepha Archduchess of Austria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_VI_of_Spain

facts.fact: Charles IV of Spain, then Prince of Asturias and heir, married his cousin Maria Luisa of Parma, daughter of Philip Duke of Parma, at La Granja on 4 September 1765; the link ends with his abdication on 19 March 1808, before her death in 1819.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (La Granja, San Ildefonso near Segovia 4 Sep 1765) his first cousin, donna MARIA LUISA di Borbone Pss of Parma, daughter of Infante don FILIPPO di Borbone Duke of Parma"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_IV_of_Spain

facts.fact: Ferdinand VII of Spain, then Prince of Asturias and heir, married his cousin Maria Antonia of Naples and Sicily, daughter of Ferdinand IV King of Naples, by proxy at Naples on 16 August 1802 and in person at Barcelona on 6 October 1802; she died on 21 May 1806.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (by proxy Naples 16 Aug 1802, in person Barcelona 6 Oct 1802) his first cousin, donna MARIA ANTONIETTA di Borbone Pss of Naples and Sicily, daughter of FERDINANDO IV King of Naples"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_VII_of_Spain

facts.fact: Ferdinand VII of Spain married his niece Maria Isabel of Portugal, daughter of John VI King of Portugal, by proxy at Cadiz on 4 September 1816 and in person at Madrid on 29 September 1816; she died on 26 December 1818.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Cadiz 4 Sep 1816, in person Madrid 29 Sep 1816) his niece, Infanta dona MARIA IZABEL de Bragança e Bourbon, daughter of JOÃO VI King of Portugal"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_VII_of_Spain

facts.fact: Ferdinand VII of Spain married his niece Maria Cristina of the Two Sicilies, daughter of Francis I King of the Two Sicilies, by proxy at Aranjuez on 9 December 1829 and in person at Madrid on 11 December 1829; the marriage ran to his death on 29 September 1833. His third wife Maria Josepha of Saxony was a niece whose father never reigned and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m fourthly (by proxy Aranjuez 9 Dec 1829 in person Madrid 11 Dec 1829) as her first husband, his niece, donna MARIA CRISTINA di Borbone Pss of the Two Sicilies, daughter of FRANCESCO I King of Two Sicilies"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/CASTILE.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_VII_of_Spain

facts.fact: Peter IV of Aragon married Maria of Navarre, daughter of Philip III King of Navarre, at Alagón on 23 July 1338 after the contract of 6 January 1337; the contract is not itself a marriage, so the link runs from 1338 to her death on 29 April 1347.
