facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (contract 6 Jan 1337, Alagón 23 Jul 1338) Infanta doña MARÍA de Navarra, daughter of FELIPE III King of Navarre Comte d'Evreux [Capet] & his wife Juana II Queen of Navarre"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ARAGON%20%26%20CATALONIA.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_IV_of_Aragon

facts.fact: Peter IV of Aragon married Eleanor of Portugal, daughter of Afonso IV King of Portugal, by proxy at Santarem on 11 June 1347 and in person at Barcelona on 18 November 1347; she died of plague on 30 October 1348.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Santarem 11 Jun 1347 in person Barcelona 18 Nov 1347) Infanta dona LEONOR de Portugal, daughter of AFONSO IV King of Portugal"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ARAGON%20%26%20CATALONIA.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_IV_of_Aragon

facts.fact: Peter IV of Aragon married Eleanor of Sicily, daughter of Peter II King of Sicily, at Valencia on 13 June 1349; the marriage ran to her death at Lleida on 20 April 1375. His fourth wife Sibila de Fortià was the daughter of a minor Catalan baron and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Valencia 13 Jun 1349) LEONOR of Sicily, daughter of PIETRO II King of Sicily [Aragon] & his wife Elisabeth of Carinthia [Görz]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ARAGON%20%26%20CATALONIA.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_IV_of_Aragon

facts.fact: John I of Aragon, then Duke of Girona and heir, married Martha of Armagnac, daughter of John I Count of Armagnac, at Barcelona on 24 June 1373; Armagnac is a separate polity with its own 1337 tag, and the marriage ran to her death at Zaragoza on 23 October 1378.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly ([Barcelona] 24 Jun 1373) MATHE d'Armagnac, daughter of JEAN [I] Comte d'Armagnac & his second wife Beatrix de Clermont"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ARAGON%20%26%20CATALONIA.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_I_of_Aragon

facts.fact: John I of Aragon married Yolande of Bar, daughter of Robert I Duke of Bar, at Montpellier/Perpignan on 2 February 1380; the marriage ran to his death on 19 May 1396.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Montpellier [Perpignan] 2 Feb 1380) YOLANDE de Bar, daughter of ROBERT I Duc de Bar & his wife Marie de France"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ARAGON%20%26%20CATALONIA.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_I_of_Aragon

facts.fact: Alfonso V of Aragon, then heir as Duke of Girona, married his cousin Maria of Castile, daughter of Henry III King of Castile, at Valencia in June 1415; he became king in 1416 and the marriage ran to his death on 27 June 1458.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Valencia Jun 1415) his first cousin, Infanta doña MARÍA de Castilla y León, daughter of ENRIQUE III King of Castile and León & his wife Katherine of Lancaster"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/ARAGON%20%26%20CATALONIA.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_V_of_Aragon

facts.fact: Afonso IV of Portugal married Beatrice of Castile, daughter of Sancho IV King of Castile, at Lisbon on 12 September 1309; the marriage predates the horizon and is counted from 1337 until his death on 28 May 1357.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Lisbon 12 Sep 1309) Infanta doña BEATRIZ de Castilla, daughter of SANCHO IV "el Bravo" King of Castile & his wife María Alfonso de Molina"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_IV_of_Portugal

facts.fact: John I of Portugal married Philippa of Lancaster, daughter of John of Gaunt Duke of Lancaster, at Oporto on 11 February 1387; her father never reigned but her half-brother Henry IV was King of England from 1399, and the rule accepts a sibling reigning after the wedding, so the link runs to her death on 19 July 1415.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Oporto Cathedral 11 Feb 1387) PHILIPPA of Lancaster, daughter of JOHN of Gaunt Duke of Lancaster & his first wife Blanche of Lancaster"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_I_of_Portugal

facts.fact: Edward I of Portugal married Eleanor of Aragon, daughter of Ferdinand I King of Aragon, at Coimbra on 4 November 1428; the marriage ran to his death on 9 September 1438.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Coimbra 4 Nov 1428) Infanta doña LEONOR de Aragón, daughter of FERNANDO I "él de Antequera" King of Aragon"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward,_King_of_Portugal

facts.fact: Afonso V of Portugal married his niece Joanna la Beltraneja, daughter of Henry IV King of Castile, while pressing her claim to Castile in 1475; the project collapsed after Toro and the link ends with the Treaty of Alcáçovas of 1479. His first wife Isabel of Coimbra was the daughter of a regent who never reigned and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "After the death of his wife, Alfonso V King of Portugal requested the hand in marriage of Infanta doña Juana de Castilla, daughter of Enrique IV King of Castile, delivered her from Villena 12 May 1475"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afonso_V_of_Portugal; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_la_Beltraneja

facts.fact: Manuel I of Portugal married Isabella of Aragon, daughter of Ferdinand II King of Aragon and Isabella I Queen of Castile, at Valencia de Alcántara in October 1497; she died at Zaragoza on 23 August 1498.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Valencia de Alcántara Oct 1497) as her second husband, Infanta doña ISABEL de Aragón, widow of Infante dom AFONSO de Portugal, daughter of FERNANDO V King of Aragon & his first wife Isabel I Queen of Castile"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_I_of_Portugal

facts.fact: Manuel I of Portugal married Maria of Aragon, daughter of Ferdinand II King of Aragon and Isabella I Queen of Castile, by proxy at Lisbon on 24 August 1500 and in person at Alcácer do Sal on 30 October 1500; she died on 7 March 1517.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Lisbon 24 Aug 1500 in person Alcacer do Sal 30 Oct 1500) his first wife's sister, Infanta doña MARÍA de Aragón, daughter of FERNANDO V King of Aragon & his first wife Isabel I Queen of Castile"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_I_of_Portugal

facts.fact: Manuel I of Portugal married Eleanor of Austria, daughter of Philip the Handsome and sister of Charles V, king of Spain from 1516, at Crato on 24 November 1518 and Lisbon on 7 March 1519; the marriage ran to his death on 13 December 1521. Her natal state is Castile-Spain under the shared Habsburg rule.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Crato 24 Nov 1518, Lisbon 7 Mar 1519) as her first husband, ELEONORE Archduchess of Austria, daughter of PHILIPP Archduke of Austria [FELIPE I King of Castile] & his wife Juana "la Loca" Queen of Castile"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manuel_I_of_Portugal

facts.fact: John III of Portugal married Catherine of Austria, daughter of Philip the Handsome and sister of Charles V, at Salamanca on 5 February 1525; the marriage ran to his death on 11 June 1557.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Salamanca 5 Feb 1525) KATHARINA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of PHILIPP Archduke of Austria [FELIPE I King of Castile] & his wife Juana "la Loca" Queen of Castile"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_III_of_Portugal

facts.fact: Peter II of Portugal married Maria Sophia Elisabeth of Pfalz-Neuburg, daughter of Philip William Elector Palatine, by proxy at Heidelberg on 2 July 1687 and in person at Lisbon on 11 August 1687; she died on 4 August 1699. His first wife Marie Françoise of Nemours belonged to a Savoy cadet duchy with no place on the map and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Heidelberg 2 Jul 1687, in person Lisbon 11 Aug 1687) MARIA SOPHIA ELISABETH Pss von Pfalz-Neuburg, daughter of PHILIPP WILHELM Elector Palatine Pfalzgraf und Herzog in Neuburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_II_of_Portugal

facts.fact: John V of Portugal married Maria Anna of Austria, daughter of Emperor Leopold I, by proxy at Neuburg on 9 July 1708 and in person at Lisbon on 27 October 1708; she died on 14 August 1754.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Neuburg bei Wien 9 Jul 1708, in person Lisbon 27 Oct 1708) MARIA ANNA JOSEPHA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor LEOPOLD I Archduke of Austria, King of Hungary and Bohemia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_V_of_Portugal

facts.fact: Joseph I of Portugal married Mariana Victoria of Spain, daughter of Philip V King of Spain, by proxy at Madrid on 27 December 1727 and in person at Elvas on 19 January 1729; the marriage ran to his death on 24 February 1777.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Madrid 27 Dec 1727, in person Elvas 19 Jan 1729) Infanta doña MARÍA ANA Victoria de Borbón y Farnesio, daughter of FELIPE V King of Spain & his second wife donna Elisabetta Farnese Pss of Parma"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_I_of_Portugal

facts.fact: John VI of Portugal married Carlota Joaquina of Spain, daughter of the future Charles IV King of Spain, by proxy at Madrid on 27 March 1785 and in person at Lisbon on 9 June 1785; he became heir as Prince of Brazil on the death of his elder brother in 1788, so the link runs from 1788 to his death on 10 March 1826.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (by proxy Madrid 27 Mar 1785, in person Lisbon 9 Jun 1785) Infanta doña CARLOTA JOAQUINA de Borbón y Borbón, daughter of Infante don CARLOS de Borbón y Sajonia Principe de Asturias [later CARLOS IV King of Spain]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_VI_of_Portugal

facts.fact: Pedro of Braganza, then Prince of Brazil and heir, married Maria Leopoldina of Austria, daughter of Emperor Francis I, by proxy at Vienna on 13 May 1817 and in person at Rio de Janeiro on 5 November 1817; the marriage ran to her death on 11 December 1826. His second wife Amélie of Leuchtenberg was the daughter of a duke who never reigned and does not qualify.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Vienna by proxy 13 May 1817 in person Rio de Janeiro 5 Nov 1817) LEOPOLDINA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of FRANZ I Emperor of Austria & his second wife donna Maria Teresa di Borbone Pss of the Two Sicilies"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/PORTUGAL.htm; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_I_of_Brazil

facts.fact: Louis IV the Bavarian married Margaret II of Hainaut, daughter of William III Count of Hainaut and Holland, at Cologne on 25 February 1324; the marriage was already in being in 1337 and ran to his death on 11 October 1347, the deposition pronounced by the electors in 1346 never being enforced. His first wife Beatrix of Schweidnitz had died in 1322.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bavaria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Koln 25 Feb 1324) MARGUERITE de Hainaut, daughter of GUILLAUME III 'le Bon' Comte de Hainaut"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BAVARIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor' (spouse list): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_IV,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Charles IV, King of Bohemia and King of the Romans, married Blanche of Valois at Prague on 8 January 1329; she was the sister of Philip VI of France, who reigned from 1328, and she died on 1 August 1348, so the marriage is counted from the 1337 horizon.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bohemia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Betrothed 1323, Prague 8 Jan 1329) BLANCHE [Marguerite] de Valois, daughter of CHARLES de France Comte de Valois"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BOHEMIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles IV, Holy Roman Emperor': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_IV,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Charles IV married Anna, daughter of Rudolf II Count Palatine of the Rhine, contracted at Bacharach on 4 March 1349 and celebrated in May 1349; the Count Palatine was an Imperial immediate prince, and she died on 2 February 1353.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bohemia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (contract Bacharach [4] Mar 1349, May 1349) ANNA Pfalzgrafin, daughter of RUDOLF II Pfalzgraf am Rhein"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BOHEMIA.htm

facts.fact: Charles IV married Anna of Schweidnitz, heiress of the Silesian duchy of Schweidnitz-Jauer, at Buda on 27 May 1353; she died on 11 July 1362.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bohemia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Buda 27 May 1353) ANNA von Schweidnitz heiress of Schweidnitz and Jauer, daughter of HEINRICH II Duke of Schweidnitz"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BOHEMIA.htm

facts.fact: Charles IV married Elisabeth of Pomerania, daughter of Bogislaw V Duke of Pomerania-Wolgast, at Krakow on 21 May 1363; she outlived him, and the marriage ended with his death on 29 November 1378.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bohemia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m fourthly (Krakow 21 May 1363) ELISABETH von Pommern, daughter of BOGISLAW V Duke of Pomerania in Hinterpommern"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BOHEMIA.htm

facts.fact: Wenceslaus IV, already crowned King of Bohemia in 1363, married Joanna of Bavaria, daughter of Albert I Duke of Bavaria-Straubing and Count of Holland, at Nuremberg on 17 November 1370; she died on 31 December 1386. The other party is the Wittelsbach duchy of Bavaria-Straubing, seated at Straubing.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bohemia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Nurnberg 17 Nov 1370) JOHANNA von Bayern, daughter of ALBRECHT Duke of Bavaria-Straubing"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BOHEMIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Wenceslaus IV of Bohemia': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wenceslaus_IV_of_Bohemia

facts.fact: Wenceslaus IV married Sophia of Bavaria, daughter of John II Duke of Bavaria-Munich, at Prague on 2 May 1389; although he was deposed as King of the Romans in 1400 he kept Bohemia, so the marriage is counted to his death on 16 August 1419.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bohemia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Prague 2 May 1389) SOPHIA von Bayern, daughter of JOHANN II Duke of Bavaria-Munich"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BOHEMIA.htm

facts.fact: Jobst of Moravia, elected King of the Romans in October 1410, had married Agnes of Opole, daughter of Boleslaw II Duke of Opole, in 1374; she outlived him, so the marriage is counted over his short reign to his death on 18 January 1411. Moravia is represented by its own 1337 tag (he was also Margrave of Brandenburg).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Moravia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (1374) AGNES [von Oppeln, daughter of BOLESLAW II Duke of Oppeln ... (-before 9 Sep 1411)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/MORAVIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Jobst of Moravia': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jobst_of_Moravia

facts.fact: Mary, crowned King (rex) of Hungary in 1382, married Sigismund of Luxembourg, Margrave of Brandenburg, in August 1385, the marriage being celebrated in person at Buda on 31 March 1387; it ended with her death in 1395. Sigismund's own margraviate of Brandenburg is the other party.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Aug 1385, in person Buda 31 Mar 1387) as her first husband, SIGMUND de Luxembourg Markgraf von Brandenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Mary, Queen of Hungary': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary,_Queen_of_Hungary

facts.fact: Sigismund, King of Hungary, contracted on 6 December 1405 and married in 1408 Barbara of Cilli, daughter of Herman II Count of Celje, a princely house holding Celje as an Imperial fief with its own 1337 tag; the marriage ran to his death on 9 December 1437.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (contract 6 Dec 1405, 1408) BARBARA of Cilli, daughter of HERMAN [II] Count of Cilli [Celje]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Barbara of Cilli': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_of_Cilli

facts.fact: Albert II of Habsburg, Duke of Austria and from 1438 King of the Romans, married Elizabeth of Luxembourg, daughter and heiress of Emperor Sigismund King of Hungary and Bohemia; the sources give either Esztergom on 28 September 1421 or Vienna on 19 April 1422, and the marriage ended with his death on 27 October 1439.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Esztergom 28 Sep 1421) ELISABETH of Hungary and Bohemia, daughter of Emperor SIGMUND"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Albert II of Germany' (spouse: Elizabeth of Luxembourg, m. 1422): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_II_of_Germany

facts.fact: Frederick III married Eleanor of Portugal, daughter of Edward King of Portugal, at Rome on 16 March 1452, on the day he was crowned Emperor; she died at Wiener Neustadt on 3 September 1467.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Rome 16 Mar 1452) Infanta dona LEONOR de Portugal, daughter of DUARTE King of Portugal"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_III,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Maximilian I, then heir to his father Frederick III, married Mary Duchess of Burgundy, daughter of Charles the Bold, at Ghent on 19 August 1477; the marriage ended with her death on 27 March 1482.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Gent 19 Aug 1477) MARIE de Bourgogne, daughter of CHARLES 'le Temeraire' Duke of Burgundy"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', 'Maximilian I: marriage and offspring': https://www.habsburger.net/en/chapter/maximilian-i-marriage-and-offspring

facts.fact: Maximilian I was married by proxy to Anne Duchess of Brittany in Rennes cathedral on 19 December 1490, but the union was annulled and Anne married Charles VIII of France in December 1491, so it is counted for 1490-1491.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Cathedrale de Rennes 19 Dec 1490, annulled by the Pope) as her first husband, ANNE Dss of Brittany"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Maximilian I married Bianca Maria Sforza, daughter of Galeazzo Maria Sforza Duke of Milan, at Hall in Tirol on 16 March 1494; she died at Innsbruck on 31 December 1510.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Hall, Tyrol 16 Mar 1494) BIANCA MARIA Sforza, widow of PHILIBERT I Duke of Savoy, daughter of GALEAZZO MARIA Sforza Duke of Milan"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Ferdinand I, Archduke of Austria, married Anna of Bohemia and Hungary, daughter of Vladislaus II, at Linz in May 1521 (the betrothal had formed part of the 1515 Vienna double wedding); she died on 27 January 1547.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Linz May 1521) ANNA Pss of Hungary & Bohemia, daughter of ULASZLO II King of Hungary"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', 'Marrying into Bohemia and Hungary with a double wedding in Vienna': https://www.habsburger.net/en/chapter/marrying-bohemia-and-hungary-double-wedding-vienna

facts.fact: Maximilian II, elected King of Bohemia in 1548, married his cousin Maria of Spain, daughter of Emperor Charles V, at Valladolid on 13 September 1548; the marriage ran to his death on 12 October 1576.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Valladolid 13 Sep 1548) his first cousin, Infanta dona MARIA of Spain Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor KARL V"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', 'Maximilian II: marriage and offspring': https://www.habsburger.net/en/chapter/maximilian-ii-marriage-and-offspring

facts.fact: Matthias, crowned King of Bohemia in 1611 and Emperor in 1612, married his niece Anna of Tyrol, daughter of Ferdinand II Archduke of Further Austria and Count of Tyrol, at Vienna on 4 December 1611; she died at Vienna on 14 December 1618.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: 'm (Vienna 4 Dec 1611) his niece, ANNA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of FERDINAND Archduke of Austria, Graf von Tirol ... (Innsbruck 4 Oct 1585-Vienna 14 Dec 1618)'; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Matthias, Holy Roman Emperor': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthias,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Ferdinand II, Emperor from 1619, married Eleonora Gonzaga, daughter of Vincenzo I Duke of Mantua, at Innsbruck on 4 February 1622; the marriage ended with his death on 15 February 1637. His first wife Maria Anna of Bavaria died in 1616, before he held any of the listed thrones, so that marriage is not counted.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Innsbruck 4 Feb 1622) ELEONORA Gonzaga Pss of Mantua, daughter of VINCENZO I Gonzaga Duke of Mantua"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', 'Ferdinand II: marriage and offspring': https://www.habsburger.net/en/chapter/ferdinand-ii-marriage-and-offspring

facts.fact: Ferdinand III, King of Hungary and Bohemia, married his cousin Maria Anna of Spain, daughter of Philip III of Spain, at Vienna on 20 February 1631; she died at Linz on 13 May 1646.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Vienna 20 Feb 1631) his first cousin, Infanta dona MARIA ANA of Spain, daughter of FELIPE III King of Spain"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', 'Ferdinand III: marriage and offspring': https://www.habsburger.net/en/chapter/ferdinand-iii-marriage-and-offspring

facts.fact: Ferdinand III married his cousin Maria Leopoldina, daughter of Leopold V Archduke of Further Austria and Count of Tyrol, at Linz on 2 July 1648; she died in childbirth on 7 August 1649.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Linz 2 Jul 1648) his first cousin, MARIA LEOPOLDINA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of LEOPOLD Archduke of Austria Graf von Tirol"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Ferdinand III married Eleonora Magdalena Gonzaga of Nevers, daughter of Charles II Gonzaga Duke of Nevers and Rethel, at Wiener Neustadt on 30 April 1651; the marriage ended with his death on 2 April 1657. Nevers is represented by its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Wiener Neustadt 30 April 1651) ELEONORA MARIA Gonzaga, daughter of CARLO II Gonzaga Duc de Nevers et de Rethel"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Leopold I married his niece Margaret Theresa of Spain, daughter of Philip IV of Spain, at Vienna in December 1666 (5 or 12 December in the sources); she died on 12 March 1673.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Vienna 5 Dec 1666) his first cousin, Infanta dona MARGARETA MARIA TERESA of Spain, daughter of FELIPE IV King of Spain"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', 'Leopold I: marriage and family': https://www.habsburger.net/en/chapter/leopold-i-marriage-and-family

facts.fact: Leopold I married Claudia Felicitas, daughter of Ferdinand Charles Archduke of Further Austria and Count of Tyrol, at Graz on 15 October 1673; she died on 8 April 1676.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Graz 15 Oct 1673) CLAUDIA FELIZITAS Archduchess of Austria, daughter of FERDINAND KARL Archduke of Austria Graf von Tirol"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Leopold I married Eleonore Magdalene of Pfalz-Neuburg, daughter of Philip William Count Palatine of Neuburg, at Passau on 14 December 1676; the marriage ran to his death on 5 May 1705. The other party is the Wittelsbach principality of Pfalz-Neuburg, seated at Neuburg on the Danube.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Passau 14 Dec 1676) ELEONORA MAGDALENA THERESA Pss von Pfalz-Neuburg, daughter of PHILIPP WILHELM Pfalzgraf von Neuburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Joseph I, King of the Romans from 1690, married Wilhelmina Amalia, daughter of John Frederick Duke of Brunswick-Luneburg in Hanover, at Vienna on 24 February 1699; the marriage ended with his death on 17 April 1711.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Vienna 24 Feb 1699) WILHELMINE AMALIE Hgn von Braunschweig-Luneburg, daughter of JOHANN FRIEDRICH Herzog von Braunschweig-Luneburg in Hannover"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', 'Joseph I: marriage and family': https://www.habsburger.net/en/chapter/joseph-i-marriage-and-family

facts.fact: Charles VI, then claimant to Spain and heir to Austria, married Elisabeth Christine of Brunswick-Wolfenbuttel, daughter of Louis Rudolph Duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbuttel, at Hietzing near Vienna on 23 April 1708; the marriage ran to his death on 20 October 1740.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Hietzing 23 Apr 1708) ELISABETH CHRISTINE Pss von Braunschweig-Blankenburg, daughter of LUDWIG RUDOLF Herzog von Braunschweig-Blankenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles VI, Holy Roman Emperor': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_VI,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Charles VII of Bavaria had married Maria Amalia of Austria, daughter of Emperor Joseph I, at Vienna on 5 October 1722; he was elected Emperor on 24 January 1742, so the marriage enters the list then and ends with his death on 20 January 1745.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Vienna 5 Oct 1722) KARL ALBRECHT Erbprinz von Bayern ... He succeeded in 1726 as KARL VII ALBRECHT Elector of Bavaria ... Elected Emperor KARL VII at Frankfurt-am-Main 24 Jan 1742"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles VII, Holy Roman Emperor': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_VII,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Maria Theresa, heiress of the Habsburg lands, married Francis Stephen Duke of Lorraine at Vienna on 12 February 1736; he was elected Emperor in 1745 and died at Innsbruck on 18 August 1765. Lorraine is represented by its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Vienna 12 Feb 1736) FRANCOIS III Duc de Lorraine ... He was elected Holy Roman Emperor at Frankfurt 13 Sep 1745"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Maria Theresa': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Theresa

facts.fact: Joseph II, then heir to his mother Maria Theresa, married Isabella Maria of Bourbon-Parma, daughter of Philip Duke of Parma, by proxy at Parma on 7 September 1760 and in person at Vienna on 6 October 1760; she died on 27 November 1763.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (by proxy Parma 7 Sep 1760 in person Vienna 6 Oct 1760) ISABELLA MARIA de Bourbon Pss of Parma, daughter of FILIPPO di Borbone Duke of Parma"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Joseph II, already King of the Romans, married Maria Josepha of Bavaria, daughter of Emperor Charles VII and Duke of Bavaria, at Schonbrunn on 23 January 1765; she died on 28 May 1767. Bavaria is meant; it has no 1337 tag, so Munich stands for it.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Munich 13 Jan 1765, in person Schonbrunn 23 Jan 1765) JOSEPHA MARIA Pss of Bavaria, daughter of Emperor KARL VII"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; 'Die Welt der Habsburger', person page 'Joseph II': https://www.habsburger.net/en/persons/habsburg-emperor/joseph-ii

facts.fact: Leopold II married Maria Luisa of Spain, daughter of Charles III King of Spain, by proxy at Madrid on 16 February 1764 and in person at Innsbruck on 5 August 1765; he was then only Grand Duke of Tuscany but became heir presumptive to the Habsburg lands on the death of his childless brother Joseph II's only child in January 1770, so the marriage enters from 1770 and runs to his death on 1 March 1792.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: 'm (by proxy Madrid 16 Feb 1764 in person Innsbruck 5 Aug 1765) Infanta dona MARIA LUISA de Borbon y Sajonia, daughter of CARLOS III King of Spain'; it records that he 'succeeded his brother, Emperor Joseph II, 20 Feb 1790': https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Leopold II, Holy Roman Emperor': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Francis II, heir of Leopold II, married his cousin Maria Teresa of Bourbon-Naples, daughter of Ferdinand IV King of Naples, by proxy at Naples on 15 August 1790 and in person at Vienna on 19 September 1790; she died on 13 April 1807. His first wife Elisabeth of Wurttemberg died on 18 February 1790, before he became heir, so that marriage is not counted.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (by proxy Naples 15 Aug 1790 in person Vienna 19 Sep 1790) his first cousin, MARIA TERESA di Borbone Pss of Naples and Sicily"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor

facts.fact: Francis II married Caroline Augusta of Bavaria, daughter of Maximilian I Joseph King of Bavaria, by proxy at Munich on 29 October and in person at Vienna on 10 November 1816; the marriage ran to his death on 2 March 1835. His third wife Maria Ludovika of Austria-Este is not counted because her father never reigned and Modena did not exist as a sovereign state at the wedding in 1808.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m fourthly (by proxy Munich 29 Oct 1816 in person Vienna 10 Nov 1816) as her second husband, CHARLOTTE AUGUSTE Pss of Bavaria ... daughter of MAXIMILIAN I King of Bavaria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Ferdinand I, heir apparent to the Austrian throne from his father's accession in 1792, married Maria Anna of Savoy, daughter of Victor Emmanuel I King of Sardinia, at Vienna on 27 February 1831; the marriage ran past the 1837 horizon.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Vienna 27 Feb 1831) MARIA ANNA CAROLINA PIA di Savoia Pss of Sardinia, daughter of VITTORIO EMANUELE I King of Sardinia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Ferdinand I of Austria': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ferdinand_I_of_Austria

facts.fact: Albert II the Wise, Duke of Austria at Vienna, married Joanna of Ferrette (Pfirt), daughter and heiress of Ulrich III Count of Ferrette, on 15 February 1324; the marriage was in being in 1337 and ended with her death on 15 November 1351. Ferrette was an Imperial immediate county with its own tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (15 Feb 1324) JEANNE de Ferrette, daughter & heiress of ULRIC [III] Comte de Ferrette [Pfirt]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Albert II, Duke of Austria': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_II,_Duke_of_Austria

facts.fact: Otto the Merry, co-Duke of Austria at Vienna from 1330, married Anna of Bohemia, daughter of John King of Bohemia, at Znaim on 16 February 1335; she died on 2 or 3 September 1338. His first wife Elisabeth of Bavaria had died in 1330 and does not fall within the horizon.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Znaim 16 Feb 1335) ANNA of Bohemia, daughter of JAN I King of Bohemia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Otto, Duke of Austria': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto,_Duke_of_Austria

facts.fact: Rudolf IV the Founder, then heir and from 1358 Duke of Austria at Vienna, married Catherine of Bohemia, daughter of Emperor Charles IV, at Vienna on 13 July 1356; the marriage ended with his death at Milan on 27 July 1365.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Vienna 13 Jul 1356) as her first husband, KATHARINA of Bohemia, daughter of Emperor KARL IV King of Germany, King of Bohemia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Rudolf IV, Duke of Austria': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudolf_IV,_Duke_of_Austria

facts.fact: Albert III with the Braid, co-Duke of Austria at Vienna from 1365, married Elisabeth of Bohemia, daughter of Emperor Charles IV, after 19 March 1366; she died on 4 September 1373.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (after 19 Mar 1366) ELISABETH of Bohemia, daughter of Emperor KARL IV King of Germany, King of Bohemia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Albert III, Duke of Austria': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_III,_Duke_of_Austria

facts.fact: Albert III married Beatrix of Nuremberg, daughter of Frederick V Burgrave of Nuremberg, at Vienna on 4 March 1375 after a contract at Passau on 11 December 1374; the marriage ran to his death on 29 August 1395. Nuremberg was an Imperial immediate burgraviate.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Contract Passau 11 Dec 1374, Vienna 4 Mar 1375) BEATRIX von Nurnberg, daughter of FRIEDRICH V Burggraf von Nurnberg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Leopold III, co-Duke of Austria at Vienna from 1365, married Viridis Visconti, daughter of Bernabo Visconti lord of Milan, at Vienna in February 1365 (the Milanese annals give the ceremony at Milan on 13 January 1366); the link ends with the Treaty of Neuberg of 25 September 1379, when he gave up Austria proper for the Inner Austrian lands, though the marriage itself lasted to his death at Sempach on 9 July 1386.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Vienna 23 Feb 1365) VERDE [Viridis] Visconti, daughter of BERNABO Visconti Signor of Milan ... The Annales Mediolanenses record the marriage 13 Jan 1366"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Leopold III, Duke of Austria': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leopold_III,_Duke_of_Austria

facts.fact: Leopold IV the Proud, who became ruler of Austria above and below the Enns at Vienna in 1406, had married Catherine of Burgundy, daughter of Philip the Bold Duke of Burgundy, at Dijon in May 1392 and Vienna on 15 August 1393; the marriage is counted over his rule of Austria proper, 1406 to his death on 3 June 1411.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Dijon May 1392, Vienna 15 Aug 1393) as her first husband, CATHERINE de Bourgogne, daughter of PHILIPPE 'le Hardi' Duke of Burgundy", and "1406 as Duke of Austria im Land ob und unter der Enns. Duke of Austria im Land ob und unter der Enns 1406": https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm

facts.fact: Albert IV the Wonder of the World, heir and from 1395 Duke of Austria at Vienna, married Joanna Sophia of Bavaria, daughter of Albert I Duke of Bavaria-Straubing and Count of Holland, at Vienna on 24 April 1390; he died on 14 September 1404. The other party is the Wittelsbach duchy of Bavaria-Straubing.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Vienna 24 Apr 1390) JOHANNA [Sophia] von Bayern, daughter of ALBRECHT I Duke of Bavaria in Niederbayern und Straubing"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Albert IV, Duke of Austria': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_IV,_Duke_of_Austria

facts.fact: John of Luxembourg, King of Bohemia, married Beatrice of Bourbon, daughter of Louis I Duke of Bourbon, contracted at the Bois de Vincennes in December 1334 with the dispensation of 9 January 1335; the marriage was in being in 1337 and ended with his death at Crecy on 26 August 1346. Bourbon holds its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Bohemia' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (contract Chateau du Bois de Vincennes Dec 1334, dispensation 3o Avignon 9 Jan 1335) as her first husband, BEATRIX de Bourbon, daughter of LOUIS de Clermont Duc de Bourbon"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/BOHEMIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'John of Bohemia': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_of_Bohemia

facts.fact: Vladislaus II, King of Bohemia from 1471, married Barbara of Brandenburg, daughter of Albert Achilles Elector of Brandenburg, at Frankfurt an der Oder on 20 August 1476; the marriage was dissolved at Rome on 7 April 1500.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Frankfurt an der Oder 20 Aug 1476, divorced Rome 7 Apr 1500) as her second husband, BARBARA von Brandenburg ... daughter of ALBRECHT ACHILLES Elector of Brandenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Vladislaus II of Hungary': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislaus_II_of_Hungary

facts.fact: Charles I of Hungary married Elisabeth of Poland, daughter of Wladyslaw I the Elbow-high King of Poland, on 6 July 1320; the marriage was in being in 1337 and ended with her death at Buda on 29 December 1380.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (6 Jul 1320) ELZBIETA of Poland, daughter of WLADYSLAW I 'Lokietek/Ellenbogen' King of Poland"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles I of Hungary': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_I_of_Hungary

facts.fact: Louis I the Great of Hungary married Margaret of Bohemia, daughter of Emperor Charles IV, by contract of 3 August 1342; she died in 1349 before 7 October.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (contract 3 Aug 1342) MARGARETA of Bohemia, daughter of Emperor KARL IV King of Germany, King of Bohemia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Louis I of Hungary': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_I_of_Hungary

facts.fact: Louis I of Hungary married Elisabeth of Bosnia, daughter of Stephen II Kotromanic Ban of Bosnia, at Krakow on 20 June 1353; the marriage ran to his death on 10/11 September 1382. Bosnia has its own 1337 tag.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (Krakow 20 Jun 1353) JELISAVETA Kotromanic of Bosnia, daughter of STJEPAN II Kotromanic Ban of Bosnia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm

facts.fact: Matthias Corvinus, King of Hungary from 1458, married Catherine of Podebrady, daughter of George King of Bohemia, contracted on 1 May 1461 and celebrated in 1463; she died on 8 March 1464.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (contract 1 May 1461, 1463) KATHARINA Podiebrad, daughter of JIRI Podiebrad King of Bohemia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Matthias Corvinus': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthias_Corvinus

facts.fact: Matthias Corvinus married Beatrice of Naples, daughter of Ferdinand I King of Naples, at Naples on 16 September 1476 and in Hungary on 13 December 1476; the marriage ran to his death on 6 April 1490.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly (Naples 16 Sep 1476, in Hungary 13 Dec 1476, repudiated) as her first husband, BEATRICE of Naples, daughter of FERRANTE I King of Naples"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm

facts.fact: Vladislaus II, elected King of Hungary in 1490, married Beatrice of Naples, widow of Matthias Corvinus and daughter of Ferdinand I King of Naples, secretly on 4 October 1490; the marriage was dissolved on 7 April 1500. His earlier marriage to Barbara of Brandenburg is counted under Bohemia.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Hungary' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (secretly 4 Oct 1490, divorced 7 Apr 1500) as her second husband, BEATRICE of Naples, widow of MATYAS Hunyadi 'Corvinus'"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/HUNGARY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Vladislaus II of Hungary': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladislaus_II_of_Hungary

facts.fact: Louis II of Hungary and Bohemia married Mary of Habsburg, granddaughter of Emperor Maximilian I, at the Vienna double wedding on 22 July 1515, when he was already crowned King of Hungary; the marriage was consummated at Prague on 13 January 1522 and ended with his death at Mohacs on 29 August 1526. Mary's brother Charles ruled the Netherlands in 1515, hence Brussels.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Austria' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (Prague 13 Jan 1522) LAJOS II King of Hungary [LUDWIG King of Bohemia], son of ULASZLO II ... MARIA Archduchess of Austria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/AUSTRIA.htm; Wikipedia, 'Louis II of Hungary' (spouse: Mary of Austria, m. 1515): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_II_of_Hungary

facts.fact: Casimir III of Poland married Anna (Aldona), daughter of Gediminas Grand Duke of Lithuania, at Kraków on 16 October 1325; a grand duke's daughter whose marriage sealed the Polish-Lithuanian alliance, counted from 1337 to her death on 26 May 1339.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (16 Oct 1325) ANNA [Aldona] of Lithuania , daughter of GEDIMINAS Grand Duke of Lithuania"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Casimir III the Great': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casimir_III_the_Great

facts.fact: Casimir III married Adelaide, daughter of Henry II Landgrave of Hesse, at Poznań on 29 September 1341; a sovereign landgrave's daughter, the marriage ended with her formal separation and return to Hesse in October 1356 and was never annulled.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (Poznań 29 Sep 1341, separated 1356) ADELHEID von Hessen , daughter of HEINRICH II ‘der Eiserne’ Landgraf Herr von Hessen"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Casimir III the Great': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casimir_III_the_Great

facts.fact: Casimir III married Hedwig, daughter of Henry III Duke of Glogau and Sagan, in spring or summer 1365; a Silesian Piast duke's daughter, the union rested on a forged dispensation while his Hesse marriage still stood and ended at his death on 5 November 1370.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m fourthly (Spring/Summer 1365) as her first husband, HEDWIG von Glogau , daughter of HEINRICH III Duke of Glogau and Sagan"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Casimir III the Great': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casimir_III_the_Great

facts.fact: Jadwiga, crowned King (rex) of Poland in 1384, married Jogaila Grand Duke of Lithuania at Kraków on 18 February 1386, he taking the crown as Władysław II; Lithuania is the natal state and the marriage ended at her death in 1399 (recorded once, as she was the reigning monarch at the wedding).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (18 Feb 1386) JADVIGA of Hungary King (rex) of Poland"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Jadwiga of Poland': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jadwiga_of_Poland

facts.fact: Władysław II Jagiełło married Anna of Cilli (Celje), daughter of Count Wilhelm of Cilli, at Kraków on 29 January 1401 (1402 in the common alternative account); an immediate Imperial county's ruling family, counted to her death in 1416.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (Krakow 29 Jan 1401) ANNA of Celje , daughter of WILHELM Graf von Cilly"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Władysław II Jagiełło' (gives 29 January 1402): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W%C5%82adys%C5%82aw_II_Jagie%C5%82%C5%82o

facts.fact: Casimir IV married Elisabeth, daughter of Albert V Duke of Austria (later Emperor Albert II), at Kraków on 10 February 1454; a Habsburg archduchess, counted to his death on 7 June 1492.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Krakow 10 Feb 1454) ELISABETH Archduchess of Austria , daughter of ALBRECHT V Duke of Austria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Casimir IV Jagiellon': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casimir_IV_Jagiellon

facts.fact: Alexander Jagiellon married Helena, daughter of Ivan III Grand Prince of Moscow, on 15 February 1495 while he was Grand Duke of Lithuania; counted from his accession as King of Poland in 1501 to his death on 19 August 1506.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (15 Feb 1495) IELENA Ivanovna of Moscow , daughter of IVAN III Vasilievich Grand Prince of Moscow"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Alexander Jagiellon': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Jagiellon

facts.fact: Sigismund I married Barbara, daughter of Stephen Zápolya Lord of Trencsén, in 1512; she qualifies through her brother John Zápolya, who reigned as King of Hungary from 1526, and the marriage ended at her death on 2 October 1515.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (28 May 1512) BORBÁLA Zápolya , daughter of ISTVÁN Zápolya Lord of Trenczin" (the year 1512 is agreed; sources differ on the day); https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Sigismund I the Old': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigismund_I_the_Old

facts.fact: Sigismund I married Bona Sforza, daughter of Gian Galeazzo Sforza Duke of Milan, on 18 April 1518; the Milanese duchy had passed to other rulers but still existed, and the marriage ended at his death on 1 April 1548.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (18 Apr 1518) BONA Sforza , daughter of GIAN GALEAZZO Sforza Duke of Milan"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Sigismund I the Old': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigismund_I_the_Old

facts.fact: Sigismund II Augustus, crowned co-king in 1530, married Elisabeth, daughter of Ferdinand I of Habsburg, on 5 May 1543; a Habsburg archduchess, counted to her death at Vilnius on 15 June 1545.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (5 May 1543) ELISABETH Archduchess of Austria , daughter of FERDINAND I"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Sigismund II Augustus': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigismund_II_Augustus

facts.fact: Sigismund II Augustus married Catherine, daughter of Ferdinand I of Habsburg, shortly after 23 June 1553; she left Poland in 1566 but the marriage was never annulled, so it is counted to his death on 7 July 1572.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m thirdly (1553, shortly after 23 Jun) as her second husband, KATHARINA Archduchess of Austria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Sigismund II Augustus': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigismund_II_Augustus

facts.fact: Anna Jagiellon, elected Queen of Poland in 1575, married Stephen Báthory Prince of Transylvania on 1 May 1576; Transylvania was a separate principality with its seat at Alba Iulia, and the marriage ended at his death on 12 December 1586.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (1 May 1576) ISTVAN Báthori Prince of Transylvania"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Anna Jagiellon': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Jagiellon

facts.fact: Sigismund III Vasa, King of Poland from 1587, married Anna, daughter of Archduke Charles II of Inner Austria, on 31 May 1592; counted to her death on 10 February 1598, his separate Swedish crown not affecting the actor.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (31 May 1592) ANNA Archduchess of Austria , daughter of KARL Archduke of Austria, Duke in Styria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Sigismund III Vasa': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigismund_III_Vasa

facts.fact: Sigismund III Vasa married Constance, daughter of Archduke Charles II of Inner Austria, on 11 December 1605; counted to her death at Warsaw on 10 July 1631.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (11 Dec 1605) KONSTANZE Archduchess of Austria , daughter of KARL Archduke of Austria, Duke in Styria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Sigismund III Vasa': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigismund_III_Vasa

facts.fact: Władysław IV Vasa married Cecilia Renata, daughter of Emperor Ferdinand II, in 1637 (12 September by the common account, 12 November in the genealogical literature); counted to her death at Vilnius on 24 March 1644.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (12 Nov 1637) CÉCILIA RENATA Archduchess of Austria , daughter of Emperor FERDINAND II"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Władysław IV Vasa' (12 September 1637): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W%C5%82adys%C5%82aw_IV_Vasa

facts.fact: Władysław IV Vasa married Marie Louise Gonzaga, daughter of Charles I Duke of Mantua, in 1646 (proxy in Paris, in person at Warsaw); counted to his death on 20 May 1648.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (10 Mar 1646) as her first husband, MARIA LUDOVICA Gonzaga Pss of Mantua , daughter of CARLO I Gonzaga Duke of Mantua"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Władysław IV Vasa': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/W%C5%82adys%C5%82aw_IV_Vasa

facts.fact: John II Casimir Vasa married his brother's widow Marie Louise Gonzaga, daughter of Charles I Duke of Mantua, on 31 May 1649; counted to her death at Warsaw on 10 May 1667.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (31 May 1649) as her second husband, MARIA LUDOVICA Gonzaga Pss of Mantua , widow of WŁADYSŁAW IV King of Poland"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'John II Casimir Vasa': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_II_Casimir_Vasa

facts.fact: Michael Korybut Wiśniowiecki, elected king in 1669, married Eleonore Maria Josefa, daughter of Emperor Ferdinand III, on 27 February 1670; counted to his death on 10 November 1673.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Poland' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (1670) as her first husband, ELEONORA MARIA JOSEFA Archduchess of Austria , daughter of Emperor FERDINAND III"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/POLAND.htm; Wikipedia, 'Michael Korybut Wiśniowiecki': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Korybut_Wi%C5%9Bniowiecki

facts.fact: Augustus II, elected King of Poland in 1697, had married Christiane Eberhardine, daughter of Christian Ernst Margrave of Brandenburg-Bayreuth, at Bayreuth on 20 January 1693; counted from his election in 1697 to his deposition in 1704 (he recovered the throne in 1709 and she died in 1727).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Saxony' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Bayreuth 20 Jan 1693) CHRISTIANE EBERHARDINE Markgräfin von Brandenburg-Bayreuth , daughter of CHRISTIAN ERNST Markgraf von Brandenburg-Bayreuth"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAXONY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Augustus II the Strong': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustus_II_the_Strong

facts.fact: Augustus III, elected King of Poland in 1733, had married Maria Josepha, daughter of Emperor Joseph I, at Vienna on 20 August 1719; counted from his election to her death on 17 November 1757.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Saxony' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Vienna 20 Aug 1719) MARIA JOSEPHA Archduchess of Austria, daughter of Emperor JOSEPH I"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SAXONY.htm; Wikipedia, 'Augustus III of Poland': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augustus_III_of_Poland

facts.fact: Valdemar IV married Helvig, daughter of Eric II Duke of Schleswig, at Sønderborg shortly before his election on 4 June 1340; Schleswig was a Danish fief but held its own 1337 tag as a separate duchy, and the marriage is counted to her death about 1374.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Sønderborg Castle shortly before 4 Jun 1340) HEILWIG von Schleswig , daughter of ERICH II Herzog von Schleswig"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Valdemar 4. Atterdag': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Valdemar_4._Atterdag

facts.fact: Eric of Pomerania, King of Denmark from 1396, married Philippa, daughter of Henry IV of England, at Lund on 25/26 October 1406; a sovereign's daughter, counted to her death at Vadstena on 5 January 1430.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "(Lund 25/26 Oct 1406) PHILIPPA of Lancaster , daughter of HENRY IV King of England"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Erik af Pommern': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Erik_af_Pommern

facts.fact: Christopher III of Bavaria married Dorothea, daughter of John Margrave of Brandenburg-Kulmbach, at Copenhagen on 12 September 1445; a Franconian Hohenzollern prince's daughter, counted to his death on 5/6 January 1448.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Copenhagen 12 Sep 1445) as her first husband, DOROTHEA von Brandenburg , daughter of JOHANN ‘dem Alchimisten’ Markgraf von Brandenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christoffer af Bayern': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christoffer_af_Bayern

facts.fact: Christian I married the widowed Dorothea, daughter of John Margrave of Brandenburg-Kulmbach, at Copenhagen on 28 October 1449; counted to his death on 21 May 1481.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Copenhagen 28 Oct 1449) as her first husband, DOROTHEA von Brandenburg , widow of CHRISTOFFER III King of Denmark"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christian 1.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christian_1.

facts.fact: Hans (John) of Denmark, heir from birth, married Christina, daughter of Ernest Elector of Saxony, at Copenhagen on 6 September 1478 after the Dresden contract of 3 December 1477; Saxony is represented by the Ernestine electoral seat, and the marriage is counted to his death on 20 February 1513.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (contract Dresden 3 Dec 1477, Copenhagen 6 Sep 1478) CHRISTINA von Sachsen , daughter of ERNST Elector of Saxony"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Wikipedia, 'John, King of Denmark': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John,_King_of_Denmark

facts.fact: Christian II married Isabella, daughter of Philip the Handsome (Philip I of Castile), on 12 August 1515; the wedding preceded Charles V's accession in Spain, so the natal court is placed at Brussels, and the marriage ended with his deposition in 1523.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (contract Enns 29 Apr 1514, 12 Aug 1515) ISABEL [Elisabeth] Archduchess of Austria , daughter of PHILIPP Archduke of Austria [FELIPE I King of Castile]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christian 2.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christian_2.

facts.fact: Frederick I, duke of Schleswig-Holstein until 1523, had married Sophia, daughter of Bogislaw X Duke of Pomerania, at Kiel on 9 October 1518; counted from his accession in 1523 to his death on 10 April 1533 (his first wife Anna of Brandenburg died in 1514 and is not counted).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (Kiel 9 Oct 1518) SOPHIE von Pommern , daughter of BOGISLAW X ‘the Great’ Duke of Pomerania"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Wikipedia, 'Frederick I of Denmark': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_I_of_Denmark

facts.fact: Christian III, heir from 1523, married Dorothea, daughter of Magnus II Duke of Saxe-Lauenburg, at Lauenburg on 29 October 1525; an Imperial immediate duke's daughter, counted to his death on 1 January 1559.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Lauenburg 29 Oct 1525) DOROTHEA von Sachsen-Lauenburg , daughter of MAGNUS II Herzog von Sachsen-Lauenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christian 3.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christian_3.

facts.fact: Frederick II married his cousin Sophia, daughter of Ulrich III Duke of Mecklenburg-Güstrow, at Copenhagen on 20 July 1572; counted to his death on 4 April 1588.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Copenhagen 20 Jul 1572) his first cousin, SOPHIE von Mecklenburg-Güstrow , daughter of ULRICH III Herzog von Mecklenburg-Güstrow"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Wikipedia, 'Frederick II of Denmark': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_II_of_Denmark

facts.fact: Christian IV married Anna Catherine, daughter of Joachim Frederick Margrave of Brandenburg, at Hadersleben on 7 December 1597; counted to her death on 8 April 1612, his later union with Kirsten Munk being with a Danish subject.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (Hadersleben 7 Dec 1597) ANNA KATHARINA von Brandenburg , daughter of JOACHIM FRIEDRICH Markgraf von Brandenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christian 4.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christian_4.

facts.fact: Frederick III, crown prince from 1647, had married Sophie Amalie, daughter of George Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, at Glückstadt on 1 October 1643; counted from his becoming heir in 1647 to his death on 9 February 1670.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Glückstadt, Schloß Glücksburg 1 Oct 1643) SOPHIE AMALIE Herzogin von Braunschweig-Lüneburg , daughter of GEORG Herzog von Braunschweig-Lüneburg-Calenberg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Wikipedia, 'Frederick III of Denmark': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_III_of_Denmark

facts.fact: Christian V, crown prince from 1648, married Charlotte Amalie, daughter of William VI Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel, on 25 June 1667; counted to his death on 25 August 1699.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (by proxy Kassel 14 May 1667, in person Nykyøbing Castle, Seeland 25 Jun 1667) CHARLOTTE AMALIE Landgräfin von Hessen-Kassel , daughter of WILHELM VI Landgraf von Hessen-Kassel"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christian 5.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christian_5.

facts.fact: Frederick IV married Louise, daughter of Gustav Adolf Duke of Mecklenburg-Güstrow, on 5 December 1695 while crown prince; counted to her death on 15 March 1721.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (Copenhagen Castle 5/15 Dec 1695) LUISE Herzogin von Mecklenburg-Güstrow , daughter of GUSTAV ADOLF Herzog von Mecklenburg-Güstrow"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Frederik 4.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Frederik_4.

facts.fact: Christian VI married Sophie Magdalene, daughter of Christian Henry Margrave of Brandenburg-Kulmbach, at Pretzsch on 7 August 1721 while crown prince; counted to his death on 6 August 1746.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Pretsch, Saxony 7 Aug 1721) SOPHIE MAGDALENE Markgräfin von Brandenburg-Bayreuth , daughter of CHRISTIAN HEINRICH Markgraf von Brandenburg-Bayreuth zu Kulmbach"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christian 6.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christian_6.

facts.fact: Frederick V, crown prince from 1730, married Louisa, daughter of George II of Great Britain, at Altona on 11 December 1743; counted to her death on 19 December 1751.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (by proxy Hannover 30 Oct 1743, in person Altona 11 Dec 1743) LOUISA Pss of Great Britain , daughter of GEORGE II King of Great Britain"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Wikipedia, 'Frederick V of Denmark': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_V_of_Denmark

facts.fact: Frederick V married Juliana Maria, daughter of Ferdinand Albert II Duke of Brunswick-Wolfenbüttel, at Frederiksborg on 8 July 1752; counted to his death on 14 January 1766.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (by proxy Schloß Salzdahlum 26 Jun 1752, in person Frederiksborg 8 Jul 1752) JULIANA MARIE Pss von Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel , daughter of FERDINAND ALBRECHT II Herzog von Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Wikipedia, 'Frederick V of Denmark': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_V_of_Denmark

facts.fact: Christian VII married his cousin Caroline Matilda, daughter of Frederick Prince of Wales and sister of George III, on 8 November 1766; counted to the divorce of 6 April 1772.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Denmark' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (by proxy St James’s Palace, London 1 Oct 1766, in person Christiansborg Castle or Frederiksborg Castle 8 Nov 1766, divorced 6 Apr 1772) his first cousin, CAROLINE MATILDA Pss of Great Britain , daughter of FREDERICK LOUIS Prince of Wales"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/DENMARK.htm; Den Store Danske, 'Christian 7.': https://denstoredanske.lex.dk/Christian_7.

facts.fact: Magnus Eriksson, King of Sweden and Norway, had married Blanche, daughter of John Count of Namur, at Bohus on 5 November 1335; a sovereign count's daughter, counted from 1337 to her death in autumn 1363.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Bohus [Tönsberghus] Castle 5 Nov 1335) BLANCHE de Namur , daughter of JEAN Comte de Namur"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Magnus IV of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnus_IV_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Erik XII, crowned joint King of Sweden in 1344, married Beatrix, daughter of Emperor Louis IV of Bavaria, before 25 October 1356; a junior king's marriage to an emperor's daughter, counted from [1355,1356] to their deaths in 1359.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (before 25 Oct 1356) BEATRIX von Bayern , daughter of Emperor LUDWIG IV King of Germany, Duke of Bavaria"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Erik XII of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_XII_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Haakon Magnusson, elected co-king of Sweden in 1362, married Margarethe, daughter of Valdemar IV of Denmark, at Copenhagen on 9 April 1363; counted from 1363 to his loss of Sweden in [1363,1364].
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Copenhagen [9] Apr 1363) MARGRETHE of Denmark , daughter of VALDEMAR IV King of Denmark"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Haakon VI of Norway': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haakon_VI_of_Norway

facts.fact: Albert of Mecklenburg, crowned King of Sweden in 1364, had married Richardis, daughter of Otto I Count of Schwerin, in 1359 after the Wismar contract of 12 October 1352; counted from his accession in 1364 to her death in 1377.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Mecklenburg' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (contract Wismar 12 Oct 1352, 1359) RICHARDIS von Schwerin , daughter of OTTO [I] Graf von Schwerin"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/MECKLENBURG.htm; Wikipedia, 'Albert, King of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert,_King_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Gustav I Vasa married Catherine, daughter of Magnus II Duke of Saxe-Lauenburg, at Stockholm on 24 September 1531; an Imperial immediate duke's daughter, counted to her death on 23 September 1535 (his later wives were Swedish noblewomen).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (Stockholm 24 Sep 1531) KATHARINA von Sachsen-Lauenburg , daughter of MAGNUS II Herzog von Sachsen-Lauenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Gustav I of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_I_of_Sweden

facts.fact: John III, king from 1569, had married Catherine Jagellon, daughter of Sigismund I of Poland, at Vilnius on 4 October 1562; counted from his accession to her death on 16 September 1583.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m firstly (Vilna 4 Oct 1562) KATARZYNA Pss of Poland , daughter of ZYGMUNT I ‘Stary’ King of Poland"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'John III of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_III_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Charles IX, regent from 1592 and king from 1604, had married Christina, daughter of Adolf Duke of Holstein-Gottorp (the Gottorp seat being in Schleswig, hence the location), on 27 August 1592; counted from his accession in 1604 to his death on 30 October 1611.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m secondly (27 Aug 1592) CHRISTINA von Holstein-Gottorp , daughter of ADOLF Herzog von Holstein-Gottorp"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles IX of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_IX_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Gustav II Adolf married Maria Eleonora, daughter of Joachim Frederick Elector of Brandenburg, at Stockholm on 26 November 1620; counted to his death at Lützen on 6 November 1632.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Stockholm 26 Nov/5 Dec 1620) MARIE ELEONORE Markgräfin von Brandenburg , daughter of JOHANN SIGISMUND Elector of Brandenburg"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Gustavus Adolphus': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustavus_Adolphus

facts.fact: Charles X Gustav married Hedwig Eleonora, daughter of Frederick III Duke of Holstein-Gottorp (seat at Gottorp in Schleswig, hence the location), at Stockholm on 24 October 1654; counted to his death on 23 February 1660.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Stockholm 24 Oct 1654) HEDWIG ELEONORE Herzogin von Holstein-Gottorp , daughter of FRIEDRICH III Herzog von Holstein-Gottorp"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles X Gustav of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_X_Gustav_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Charles XI married Ulrika Eleonora, daughter of Frederick III of Denmark, at Skottorp on 6 May 1680; counted to her death on 26 July 1693.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Skottorp near Helsingborg 6 May 1680) ULRIKA ELEONORA Pss of Denmark , daughter of FREDERIK III King of Denmark"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles XI of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_XI_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Ulrika Eleonora, recognised as the closest heir and regent in 1713 and queen regnant from 1718, had married Frederick Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel in 1715; counted from 1715 to her death on 24 November 1741, he reigning with her from 1720.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (Stockholm 4/15 Apr 1715) as his second wife, FRIEDRICH Landgraf von Hessen-Kassel , son of KARL Landgraf von Hessen-Kassel"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Ulrika Eleonora of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulrika_Eleonora_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Adolf Frederick, elected crown prince of Sweden in 1743, married Louisa Ulrika, daughter of Frederick William I of Prussia, in 1744 (proxy at Berlin 17 July, in person at Drottningholm 29 August); counted to his death on 12 April 1771.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (by proxy Berlin 17 Jul 1744, in person Drottningholm 29 Aug 1744) LUISE ULRIKE Pss of Prussia , daughter of FRIEDRICH WILHELM I King of Prussia"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Adolf Frederick of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Frederick_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Gustav III married Sophia Magdalena, daughter of Frederick V of Denmark, on 4 November 1766; counted to his assassination on 29 March 1792.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (by proxy Christiansborg castle, Copenhagen 1 Oct 1766, in person Stockholm 4 Nov 1766) SOPHIE MAGDALENA Pss of Denmark , daughter of FREDERIK V King of Denmark"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Gustav III of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_III_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Gustav IV Adolf married Frederica, daughter of Charles Louis Hereditary Prince of Baden, at Stockholm on 31 October 1797; she qualifies as sister of Charles Grand Duke of Baden from 1811, and the marriage ended with his deposition in 1809.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (by proxy Stralsund 6 Oct 1797, in person Stockholm 31 Oct 1797, divorced Basel 17 Feb 1812) FRIEDERIKE Pss von Baden , daughter of KARL LUDWIG Erbmarkgraf von Baden"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Gustav IV Adolf of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gustav_IV_Adolf_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Charles XIII, king from 1809, had married Hedwig Elisabeth Charlotte, daughter of Frederick August Duke of Oldenburg, at Stockholm on 7 July 1774; counted from his accession in 1809 to his death on 5 February 1818.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, 'Sweden' (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v. : "m (by proxy Wismar 22 Jun 1774 in person Stockholm 7 Jul 1774) HEDWIG SOPHIE CHARLOTTE Pss von Holstein-Gottorp , daughter of FRIEDRICH AUGUST Herzog von Holstein-Gottorp"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/SWEDEN.htm; Wikipedia, 'Charles XIII of Sweden': https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_XIII_of_Sweden

facts.fact: Simeon (Semion) the Proud, Grand Prince of Vladimir and Moscow from 1340, had married Anastasia (Aigusta), daughter of Gediminas Grand Duke of Lithuania, in 1333; a grand duke's daughter whose match sealed a truce with Lithuania, counted from 1337 to her death on 11 March 1345.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (1333) ANASTASIA [Aigusta] of Lithuania, daughter of GEDIMINAS Grand Duke of Lithuania ... (-11 Mar 1345). Her marriage was arranged to confirm a truce in relations between Lithuania and Moscow"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm

facts.fact: Simeon the Proud married secondly in 1345 Iefpraxia, daughter of Fedor Prince of Dorogobuzh and Viazma, and repudiated her in 1346; Viazma was a separate Rurikid appanage principality with its own 1337 tag, so the princess counts, but the union lasted only about a year.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m secondly (1345, divorced 1346) as her first husband, IEFPRAXIA Fedorovna, daughter of FEDOR Prince of Dorogobuzh and Viazma"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm

facts.fact: Simeon the Proud married thirdly in 1347 Maria, daughter of Aleksandr Mikhailovich Grand Prince of Tver, a rival grand principality with its own 1337 tag; the marriage, meant to subordinate Tver, ended at his death from plague on 26 April 1353.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m thirdly ([1347]) MARIA Aleksandrovna of Tver, daughter of ALEKSANDR Mikhailovich Prince of Tver ... (-17 Mar 1397)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm

facts.fact: Ivan II, then heir presumptive to his childless elder brother Simeon and Grand Prince from 1353, married in 1341 Feodosia, daughter of Dmitry Romanovich Prince of Briansk, a separate Rurikid principality with its own 1337 tag; the marriage ended with her death in autumn 1342.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (1341) FEDOSIA Dmitrievna of Briansk, daughter of DMITRY Romanovich Prince of Briansk (-Autumn 1342)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm

facts.fact: Dmitry Donskoy, Grand Prince of Moscow from 1359, married Eudoxia, daughter of Dmitry Konstantinovich Grand Prince of Suzdal-Nizhny Novgorod, on 18 January 1367 to seal an alliance; Suzdal-Nizhny Novgorod was a separate grand principality with its own 1337 tag (seat Nizhny Novgorod), and the marriage lasted to his death on 19 May 1389.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (18 Jan 1367) IEVDOKIA Dmitrievna of Suzdal, daughter of DMITRY Konstantinovich Prince of Suzdal, former Grand Prince of Vladimir ... (-7 Jul 1407)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm

facts.fact: Vasily I, Grand Prince of Moscow from 1389, married Sophia, daughter of Vytautas Grand Duke of Lithuania, on 9 January 1391; a grand duke's daughter, the match bound Moscow to its strongest western neighbour and ended at his death in February 1425.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (9 Jan 1391) SOFIA of Lithuania, daughter of VYTAUTAS [Witold] Prince of Lithuania [later Grand Duke of Lithuania] & his second wife Anna Sviatoslavna of Smolensk (1371-15 Jun 1453)"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm

facts.fact: Ivan III, co-regent and designated heir of Vasily II, married Maria, daughter of Boris Aleksandrovich Grand Prince of Tver, on 4 June 1452 as part of Tver's support against Shemiakha; Tver was still a separate grand principality with its own tag, and the marriage ended at her death in April 1467.
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m firstly (Betrothed 1446, 4 Jun 1452) MARIA Borisovna of Tver, daughter of BORIS Aleksandrovich Grand Prince of Tver ... ([1442]-22/27 Apr 1467). This marriage was agreed as part of the arrangement under which Tver agreed to support Grand Prince Vasily II"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm

facts.fact: Peter III, declared heir to Empress Elizabeth in 1742 and emperor in 1762, married Sophie Augusta Frederica, daughter of Christian August Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, an Imperial immediate principality, at St Petersburg on 1 September 1745; counted from the wedding to his deposition on 5 July 1762 (the same marriage is Catherine II's, so only one fact is recorded).
facts.source: Foundation for Medieval Genealogy, Medieval Lands, "RUSSIA, Rurik" (Charles Cawley, ed.), s.v.: "m (St Petersburg 1 Sep 1745) SOPHIE AUGUSTA FRIEDERIKE Pss von Anhalt-Zerbst, daughter of CHRISTIAN AUGUST Fürst von Anhalt-Zerbst ... (Stettin 2 May 1729-St Petersburg 17 Nov 1796). She was baptised [Orthodox]"; https://fmg.ac/Projects/MedLands/RUSSIA,%20Rurik.htm
